SPECIFIC: Parameters per leg i: pivot P_i (S-local point at r_skin in the rest pose + 8 mm along an S-local direction); crank axis n_i (S-local unit, default the outward skin normal at P_i, tilt 0-40 deg); crank radius rc_i; ball b_i (arm point (s, th, r_skin + 6)); strut length L_i (default: median over poses of |Rs P_i - Rh b_i|); branch br_i. Per pose: P = Rs P_i, n = Rs n_i, Bv = Rh b_i; take an orthonormal pair e1, e2 perpendicular to n; X = Bv - P, x = X.e1, y = X.e2. rhs = (rc^2 + |X|^2 - L^2) / (2 rc sqrt(x^2 + y^2)); |rhs| > 1 means no closure (None); otherwise phi = atan2(y, x) + br acos(rhs) and the crank tip is c = P + rc (cos phi e1 + sin phi e2). Strut frame: e_s = (Bv - c)/L, w_s = unit(e_s x n) (the strut's U axis is perpendicular to both the crank axis and the chord), third axis e_s x w_s. The strut centreline is defined in this frame by 3 control offsets along the chord (bulging toward or away from GH), fitted by EF on rays from GH through its samples (aim skin + 4 mm). Conditioning: m_i = Bv x e_s (moment of a unit strut force about GH); if sigma_min([m_1 m_2 m_3]) / 100 mm < 0.15, the pose is singular (None). The crank-strut angle must stay >= 15 deg from collinear, i.e. acos(|e_s . (c - P)/rc|) >= 15 deg. Metal: crank plate 12 mm wide x rc at the hub's upper level (+3.15); a U keep-out sphere O12 at c; strut samples along its skin-facing generator (O6); a ball cup O14 x 10 at Bv; the O20 crank hubs. Report sigma_min percentiles and the dead-centre margins. Telescoping variant: drop the cranks; |P - Bv| is the active coordinate, the strut is straight (minimum length = closed length of the telescope), with a U at P and a ball at Bv.
sweep_params: Pivot sites (3 x 2 angles, plus distance 55-130 mm from GH); crank axis tilt 0-40 deg; crank radius 20-55 mm; ball sites s 80-180 / th -90..+90 / standoff 4-12 mm; branches; strut bulge offsets; crank vs telescoping legs. Objectives: 5th percentile of sigma_min first (feasibility), then reach and inband14.
prior_art: Delta and 3-RUS parallel robots (Clavel 1988). Parallel shoulder exoskeletons that use the wearer's joint to close the loop: BONES (Klein et al. 2008/2010). Kinematic-compatibility designs (Schiele & van der Helm 2006). Curved struts on U-joints around a shoulder: none known.

name: 2R pointing boom + humeral-twist C-arc on the arm (2 DOF at the shoulder, twist farther down)
topology: S -> J1: ACTIVE R (O20 hub), axis u1 through GH whose line stays >= ~32 deg from every humerus direction: S lat ~46 / lon ~32, i.e. a hub on the top-front of the acromion / lateral clavicle, 52 deg from p* -> link 1 (a12 = 90) -> J2: ACTIVE R (O20 hub), axis u2 = unit(u1 x h) -> link 2 = pointing boom along the arm in the frame (h, u2). It follows the humerus direction but not its axial rotation -> J3: ACTIVE R about the humerus axis h, realised as a boom-fixed C-shaped arc rail around the arm (thin-section ring segment, 150-200 deg, at s 140-200 mm, constant radius = arm skin + 6) carrying a short arm-fixed carriage (25 deg) on the user's cuff saddle. Azimuth-elevation-roll: the user's suggestion of 2026-10-14 ('put upper arm rotation in its own DOF farther down').
dof_reasoning: A classic 3R gimbal (J1 perpendicular to J2 perpendicular to J3 = h), non-redundant. The humerus direction gives J1 and J2 in closed form, and the arm's twist sets the carriage position on the arc; nothing floats. Measured: the best J1 line within 70 deg of the dome stays >= 32 deg from every humerus direction over the workspace (38-40 deg on the clips), so the singular margin is ~32 deg. The user's cuff slides remain outside the count.
description: Only two joints sit over the shoulder, and the twist lives on the stable lateral arm strip (skin 55-65 mm from the axis laterally, 3-6 mm change at s 120-210). Overhead-first trade-off: the J1 site is the one place the humerus line keeps away from, the top-front of the acromion. But that skin bunches overhead (30-45 deg from p*, toward lateral/anterior: skin 36-79 mm from GH, with arm skin present in 7-14 % of poses). REST: J1 is on the top-front of the shoulder; link 1 is a 90 deg arc over the lateral shoulder to J2; the boom runs down the lateral arm to the C-arc around mid-humerus, which opens medially. OVERHEAD: J1 sits near the raised arm's root; link 1 and J2 arc over the top of the shoulder; the boom runs along the raised arm, and the arc at mid-arm is clear of everything. ACROSS THE BODY: the boom stays on the arm, and the C-arc's medial opening has to face the chest. BEHIND THE BACK: internal rotation drives the carriage toward one end of the arc.
why_better: Two shoulder joints instead of three, as the user suggested. The twist joint is off the shoulder, on the arm, so the transition carries only link 1, J2 and the boom root. The ~32 deg singular margin is about twice the 12.5-20 deg in FINDINGS. The closed-form kinematics are trivial.
main_risk: Twist travel, measured: relative to the boom, the arm turns through 124 deg over the fit clips and 295 deg over the everyday workspace. A C-arc that must stay open on the trunk side cannot exceed ~150-200 deg, and FINDINGS found an arm-fixed arc body-free over only 124-130 deg, so a large share of the workspace may be out of reach (R16). A circular arc around a non-round arm sees 13.5-25 mm of skin-radius change over 120 deg, so it stands off on the thin sectors. The J1 site is on bunching skin. The boom is a long cantilever under MVP2 moments.
unpowered_and_mvp2: Unpowered: arm-driven and non-redundant; the carriage rolls on the arc (crossed rollers or V-wheels on a Ti arc); nothing sags. MVP2: J1 and J2 are v5 hubs with drums; J3 is driven by a cable along the arc (the arc is the drum) with an encoder strip on it.

SPECIFIC: Per pose: h = Rh a, u = Rs u1, v = br unit(u x h); record None if angle(h, +-u) < 10 deg. Boom frame (h, v, h x v). Twist psi = atan2(z . (h x v), z . v) with z = Rh z_L. The carriage's arm-local angle th_c is fixed, so its boom-frame angle is psi + th_c; record None if that leaves [th_mid - (travel - 25)/2, th_mid + (travel - 25)/2]. Metal: J1 hub at u (r1 = r_skin + 3); link-1 ribbon u -> v (EF in the frame (u, v)); J2 hub at v (EF radius); the boom ribbon in the boom frame along the arm from J2 to the arc at boom angle th_b around h (EF on rays from GH near the shoulder; beyond s > 80, use radial lines from the humerus axis: rho = max over poses of arm skin radius + 2). name: Non-concurrent 3R on skin-normal hubs with a passive self-aligning cuff (2 slides)
topology: S -> J1: ACTIVE R (O20 hub on the dome; its axis is the local outward skin normal, which misses GH by 5-25 mm) -> link 1 (a flatter strap following the skin between hub centres) -> J2: ACTIVE R (hub on the posterior acromion / posterior deltoid, axis skin-normal in the home pose) -> link 2 -> J3: ACTIVE R (hub on the lateral arm strip, axis skin-normal) -> passive self-aligning cuff module: P_s, a rolling miniature rail along the humerus axis (+-20 mm), plus P_t, a rolling rail tangential across the lateral arm (+-15 mm) -> user's cuff. The axes do not meet.
dof_reasoning: The end link's orientation depends only on the axis DIRECTIONS (R_end = Rot(d1, q1) Rot(d2, q2) Rot(d3, q3)). So the three active angles are exactly those of a spherical chain with the same directions (closed-form TC solve), and the encoders read the arm orientation exactly, whatever the slides do. The translation mismatch e produced by the axis offsets goes into the two passive cuff slides, whose positions the arm sets by closure through the cuff: they are the user's 'passive self-aligning slides at the cuff', outside the count. The radial (skin-normal) part of e cannot be absorbed and must stay <= 3 mm by design (a sweep constraint). Nothing is undriven: the slides move only when the arm moves them.
description: Freed from concurrency, each hub can sit flat on stable skin with its axis along the local skin normal (minimal rim stand-off on sloping skin), and the links become flatter straps between hubs instead of arcs on a sphere around GH. The same slides absorb the real GH-vs-scapula translation (R10; the published bone-pin data in FINDINGS show +35 mm superior at 90 deg scaption), which no spherical family can. REST: J1 is on the dome, J2 on the back of the acromion, J3 on the lateral arm; the slides are centred. OVERHEAD: the arm turns ~110 deg relative to the scapula. name: Spherical five-bar pointer (two base motors) + arm turret roll

J3 is a thin-section turret ring on the lateral arm strip, with arm-fixed axis j_o through GH (s 110-150, th -20..+40). A spherical 5R closed loop (2-DOF pointing of w) plus a coaxial roll.

description: Overhead-first: both pointing motors sit on stable scapula skin, one on the dome (never visited by the humerus), one on the infraspinous fossa. The roll is a turret ring on the stable lateral strip: continuous rotation, no C-arc travel limit, no neck. REST: leg A runs from the dome over the lateral shoulder, leg B from the back over the posterior deltoid, meeting at the turret on the lateral arm. OVERHEAD: the turret rises beside the head; leg A folds over the dome and leg B along the back of the raised arm. ACROSS THE BODY: leg B stretches across the back of the shoulder. REST: the arm hangs ~150-178 deg from u0, and three leg pairs fan down over the front, side and back of the deltoid to three platform hubs around the arm at the deltoid insertion. name: Breathing hubs: cam-slaved radial joint stages on a spherical 3R
topology: Scapula base (S) -> J1: R hub, ACTIVE, axis b through GH, base-fixed, fixed radius -> link 1: rigid Ti strap whose distal end is a radial parallelogram stage (two 0.6 x 12 mm Ti leaves, 30 mm long, 4 mm apart, tangent to the sphere at J2; passive P along p2, 8-15 mm travel) -> J2: R hub, ACTIVE, axis p2 through GH; its pin block floats along p2 -> link 2: rigid strap with a radial parallelogram stage at each end (the J2 end follows the J2 block, the J3 end follows the arm-hub block) -> J3: R hub, ACTIVE, axis W (arm-fixed) through GH -> arm-hub block on BOTTOM's neck, itself on a radial parallelogram stage (passive P along W). Lift drivers: a groove face cam (O32 x 3 mm ramp ring) fixed to the base around J1, an MR63 follower on link 1's root and a 1.5 mm Ti pushrod along link 1 to a bell crank on the J2 stage, so lift2 = c2(q1); a groove face cam on link 2's J3 end read by a follower on BOTTOM's stage, so lift3 = c3(q3). Optional level 2: each link's mid-span is a 3-segment flexure four-bar slaved to the same cam (mid-span lift m_k(q)). Active: q1, q2, q3. Passive: lift2 and lift3, both set by cams.
dof_reasoning: Every axis passes through GH, so translating a pin block along its own axis changes no axis direction and no joint angle. The radial lifts are therefore kinematically free, and the three hub encoders alone give the arm's orientation: the lifts never need to be measured or powered. Each lift is positively driven by a groove cam whose input is an adjacent joint angle. The arm turns q1 or q3 and the cam sets the lift (closure), so no lift can sag or flop unpowered (R17), and none needs a motor in MVP2. The stages are parallelograms, so the pin blocks translate without tilting their axes. The parasitic tangential shift, delta^2 / (2 x 30 mm) = 1.1-3.8 mm at 8-15 mm of lift, is GH misalignment that the user's passive cuff slides absorb.
description: It looks like the current 3R: a base hub on the acromion top, the J2 hub, an arm hub on the lateral deltoid and two strap links. The difference is that the link ends are short double-leaf stages, and the J2 hub and the arm hub 'breathe': each rides 2-4 mm over its skin and rises by up to 15 mm only where the cam profile says that q1 (or q3) needs it. Rest (arm hanging): J2 sits over the posterior-superior shoulder at its lowest lift, and the whole mechanism is 2-8 mm off the skin. Overhead (142-150 deg): this is where the final's J2 hub sinks 2.7-6.7 mm into the back over the medial scapula and link 1 crosses the acromion. Here the J1 cam has lifted J2 by the 10-15 mm it needs, only in that q1 range, and the links S-bend down to J1 and J3. Across-body (Wash opposite shoulder): J2 swings anterior-superior and its lift follows the cam's envelope for that q1. The arm hub lifts with q3 over the bunched deltoid. Behind-back (Reach back pocket): q3 is near its internal-rotation end, and the arm hub and link 2's J3 end ride the c3 lift over the posterior deltoid. The J1 hub and its cam ring stay on low-motion scapula skin (1.8 mm of skin motion).
why_better: The R1 decomposition (docs/research/proximity_levers.md) puts 87 % of the loss in three zones. The J2 zone alone is 18 points, and no rigid shape can recover it (5 % even when every point is 'lowered'): J2 sweeps skin 58-93 mm from GH, and a perfect rigid reshaping caps R1 at 56 %. Rigidity is the cause, and in a spherical chain the radial coordinate along each axis is free. So letting the hub heights follow the pose costs no kinematics: follow and reach stay the baseline's (~98 % / ~78 %). Meanwhile the 'motion' part of the loss is removed as far as it correlates with q1/q3: 12.2 mm at J2, 10.4 mm at the arm hub and 4.6 mm on link 2. If the need were a function of the cam input alone, the upper bound would be the evaluator's ceiling (86-90 %).
main_risk: The skin need under J2 is a function of the whole pose, not of q1 alone. If, at a fixed q1, the need still spreads by more than 12 mm (the arm is under J2 in some poses and not in others), the cam must take each bin's maximum and most of the gain disappears. The bench's per-bin spread answers this in minutes. Second risk: parts and mass (three stages, two cams, a pushrod and a bell crank) within a 500 g budget, and the stages must stay stiff in tangential bending and torsion under MVP2's ~10 N.m (leaf sizing). A skin-referenced follower (a skid on the base layer) would remove the first risk entirely, but it touches the skin, which the user's rule excludes.
unpowered_and_mvp2: MVP1: the hubs keep today's v5 rolling pairs (MR117 x2). The cam followers are MR63 bearings in groove cams (positive drive, no spring), or spring-preloaded at 3-5 N. The reaction on the arm is preload x cam slope (<= 12 mm/rad), about 0.05 N.m, 20x under R17's 1 N.m. Nothing can drop. Sensing: the user's encoders on J1-J3 only; the lifts need none because they do not affect orientation. MVP2: each hub keeps its v5 rim drum and remote-motor cable exactly as on the baseline; the cams and stages stay passive. To check: the hub tilt moments pass through the parallelogram leaves.
model_spec: Bench: B = CB.Bench(). Per pose i: F = B.frames(i); Rs, Rh = F['S'][0], F['H'][0]; Q = Rs.T @ Rh (the arm in scapula coords). Compute in scapula coords and map to thorax with x_T = Rs @ x_S: GH is the origin, there is no translation, and the trunk translation is already in the posed skin. Conventions (pipeline/conformal/gpu/band_impl.py): bvec(az,el) = [-cos el cos az, sin el, cos el sin az] (scapula frame); w_dir(d,az) = [sin d sin az, -cos d, sin d cos az] (humerus frame, long axis -y). Port circ_int (the intersection of two circles on the unit sphere) and tri_ok to numpy. Chain (the final, pipeline/full-exo/designs/cad_r18_n3_s1392_1_f300/design.json): b = bvec(32.55, 80.56), W0 = w_dir(71.38, 4.78), a1 = 77.41 deg, a2 = 81.45 deg, branch -1. Per pose: p3 = Q @ W0; p2 = circ_int(b, a1, p3, a2, -1). Return None if there is no intersection or tri_ok fails with a 10 deg margin. Joint angles: q1 = atan2(p2.f, p2.e) with e = unit(b x [0,1,0]) and f = b x e. q3 = the signed angle about p3 from the projection of p2 to the projection of Q @ r0, with r0 = unit(W0 x [1,0,0]). Skin radius rho_i(d) along a unit direction d: the first hit of the ray from the origin on trimesh.Trimesh(*B.skin(i)) (ray.intersects_location, minimum norm). Precompute it on a 1 deg direction grid (latitude -60..90 around the shoulder) per pose and interpolate. Metal (O20 v5 hub, docs/HARDWARE.md): each hub is a lower-plate disc of radius 10 mm with its skin face at F_k (radius from GH along the axis); the upper member's underside is at F_k + 3.15 and the cap crown at F_k + 12.25. Sample the lower disc face on a 2 mm grid; use the stack for collisions only. Links are 14 mm wide strips along the great-circle arc between the two hub rims, sampled every 2 mm along x 3 across, each sample at radius r(u), u in [0,1]. Breathing: F_1 is constant (fitted); F_2(i) = F2_0 + c2(q1(i)); F_3(i) = F3_0 + c3(q3(i)). Need of a flat disc on axis p at pose i: n(i) = max over the disc's in-plane offsets o of rho_i(unit(F p + o)) * (unit(F p + o).p) + 2 mm (two fixed-point iterations on F). Cam fit: bin q1 in 4 deg bins over the kinematically taken poses; env(bin) = max n2(i) over the bin and its two neighbours; F2_0 = max(min env, max env - T) with T = 15 mm; c2 = clip(env - F2_0, 0, T). Then enforce |dc/dq| <= 12 mm/rad (38 deg pressure angle at a 15 mm cam radius) by a forward and a backward running-max pass. Fit c3 the same way over q3 at the arm hub. Link 1 profile: r1(u,i) = R1(u) + s(u) c2(q1(i)) with s = 3u^2 - 2u^3, where R1(u) = max over taken poses of [rho + 2 mm of the strip samples at u (max of the 3 across) - s(u) c2(q1(i))]. Link 2: r2(u,i) = R2(u) + (1 - s(u)) c2(q1(i)) + s(u) c3(q3(i)), with R2 fitted the same way. Level 2: add 4u(1-u) m_k(q), with m_k fitted like c (link 1 on q1, link 2 on q3) and 10 mm of travel. Cam rings are metal too: a base-fixed annulus at r 12-16 mm around J1 at F_1, and a BOTTOM-fixed annulus around J3. A pose is taken if the chain closes, every lift is within its travel, and all metal has B.dist >= 0 (B.record handles this). Controls: c2 = c3 = 0 must reproduce the rigid baseline model; report both. Fit on the clip poses plus the even workspace poses and also report on the odd workspace poses (the fit is otherwise in-sample). Key diagnostic: the per-bin spread of n2 at fixed q1 (median and p90 of max - min within each bin).
sweep_params: Which radial coordinates breathe: {J2}, {J2, J3}, or {J2, J3 + link mid-span morph}. J2 cam input: q1, q2, or both. Lift travel T 8-20 mm; slope limit 6-15 mm/rad. Base chains: r18 s1392 #1 (the final), r20 s1414 #4, agD_n3_wbox_1 (W boxed near (100, -7)). Singular margin 8-15 deg. Fit/evaluate split over the workspace poses.
prior_art: None known for exoskeletons. Related: passive translational self-alignment in exoskeletons (Schiele and van der Helm, IEEE TNSRE 2006; Stienen et al., IEEE T-RO 2009). Parallel-leaf flexure stages and positive-drive groove face cams are standard precision-engineering parts.

name: Conical CORE chain: rolling-contact joints in a single layer
topology: Scapula base -> J1: a conical rolling-contact pair (CORE). The base-fixed cone segment C1A (axis c1A) and the link-1 cone segment C1B (axis c1B) have equal half-angles beta, their apex at GH, and touch along a generator. Three crossed 0.1 x 4 mm Ti or 17-7PH bands in a figure-8 hold them; ACTIVE coordinate: rolling angle psi1 -> link 1 (a 14 mm Ti strap in the same layer as the discs) -> J2: CORE pair C2A (link 1) / C2B (link 2), ACTIVE psi2 -> link 2 -> J3: CORE pair C3A (link 2) / C3B (the arm end on BOTTOM's neck), ACTIVE psi3 -> arm end. There are no pins and no stacked plates: each joint is two O14 x 4.5 mm discs side by side. Variant: unequal cones per joint (rolling ratio != 1).
dof_reasoning: Each CORE pair is a one-parameter rolling motion: the crossed bands prevent slip and keep the surfaces in contact. So each joint has exactly one coordinate psi_k, measured in MVP1 and driven in MVP2. All cone apexes are at GH, so every relative motion fixes GH (a spherical chain): 3 coordinates for the arm's 3 rotations and nothing spare. The bands are elastic elements, not coordinates, and there is no idle body (no idler rollers).
description: A flat chain: strap - disc|disc - strap - disc|disc - strap. Each joint is a pair of Ti discs (O14, 4.5 mm tall including the band) lying side by side in the skin's tangent plane, wrapped in a figure-8 of three thin bands. The links leave each disc on its far side, all in the same 4.5-5 mm layer. When a joint turns by ~2psi, the distal disc rolls psi around the proximal one (coin around coin), so the distal link's root orbits the joint instead of turning on a pin (psi <= 85 deg). Rest: the J1 pair is on the acromion top (scapula), the J2 pair over the posterior-superior shoulder and the J3 pair on the lateral deltoid. With discs 2-4 mm off the skin, every metal point is within about 9 mm of it. Overhead: the J1 and J2 pairs have rolled 50-80 deg and the straps fan around the pairs. No hub cap sits 12 mm up, so where the final's link-1 J2 hub went 2.7-6.7 mm under the back skin at 142-150 deg, the disc pair sits 7 mm lower. Across-body and behind-back: the same rolling; each orbiting disc sweeps an annulus of radius 2rho = 14 mm around its partner, which is the footprint risk.
why_better: It removes the stacked joint that every 3R build carries. Lower plate + upper hub + cap reach 12.25 mm above the lower face (v5); that pushes upper members and caps out of band and puts hubs under the trunk or arm skin (joint size alone is worth ~20 points of workspace, FINDINGS). A CORE pair is ~4.5 mm tall and needs no overlap between its two members, so the whole chain is a single layer and stays inside 2-10 mm wherever its discs sit at 2-5 mm. CORE joints are also routinely cable-driven, which fits MVP2.
main_risk: These are not rolling bearings, so the user must accept rolling-contact joints. A pair carries compression at the contact. Separation and tilt moments ride on the bands alone: MVP1's <= 0.5 N.m of tilt means ~70 N of band load at rho 7 mm, and MVP2's 10 N.m is impossible without a retainer (a spherical cap or a lipped track). The two-disc footprint (28 x 14 mm) and the orbiting distal disc may cost reach, since hub diameter was worth 20 points. The cone apexes must meet GH within ~1 mm. Bands fatigue. Sensing a rolling joint is non-trivial: the relative angle is ~2psi, readable by a hall sensor on one disc and a magnet ring on its partner, or by IMUs.
unpowered_and_mvp2: MVP1: rolling contact has near-zero friction (rolling resistance only) and the bands add an elastic torque under 0.01 N.m. There are only three joints, so nothing sags; R17 should be met at least as well as with bearings. Sensing is the user's: a hall/magnet pair across each disc pair. MVP2: one Bowden or Dyneema cable per joint, wrapped over its two rolling surfaces (the classic CORE drive), from a remote motor. The band set must be uprated, or a retaining cap added, for 10 N.m.
model_spec: Bench: B = CB.Bench(); Q_i = Rs.T @ Rh from B.frames(i); scapula coords mapped to thorax by Rs; bvec, w_dir and circ_int as in band_impl.py (port circ_int to numpy). Reference chain: the final 3R (b = bvec(32.55, 80.56), W0 = w_dir(71.38, 4.78), a = 77.41 / 81.45 deg, branch -1). Compute its closed-form IK over all bench poses as a product of exponentials about a reference config, take each joint's range and its middle q_mid, and set Q0 = the arm orientation at q_mid. The axes at that config, m1, m2, m3 (scapula coords), are the joint mean axes. CORE pair k: choose a unit n_k perpendicular to m_k. Default: the in-plane direction from the proximal to the distal member at that joint; sweep its angle about m_k. beta_k = atan(rho / F_k), with rho = 7 mm and F_k the joint's skin-face radius (start from the baseline hub faces, ~75 / 95 / 86 mm). Cone axes: cA_k = cos(beta) m_k - sin(beta) n_k (proximal body) and cB_k = cos(beta) m_k + sin(beta) n_k (distal body). Kinematics: for equal cones the spin equals the precession, so in product-of-exponentials form R(psi) = Rot(cA1,psi1) Rot(cB1,psi1) Rot(cA2,psi2) Rot(cB2,psi2) Rot(cA3,psi3) Rot(cB3,psi3) Q0, and this must equal Q_i. For unequal cones the spin angle is psi sin(betaA) / sin(betaB). Body poses: B0 = I; B1 = Rot(cA1,psi1) Rot(cB1,psi1); B2 = B1 Rot(cA2,psi2) Rot(cB2,psi2); B3 = B2 Rot(cA3,psi3) Rot(cB3,psi3). IK: scipy.optimize.least_squares on the 3-vector Rotation.from_matrix(R(psi) @ Q_i.T).as_rotvec(). Seeds: psi = (q - q_mid) / 2 from the baseline closed form for the same pose, plus +-40 deg seeds. Accept if the residual is < 1e-6 rad and |psi_k| <= 85 deg. Metal is defined in the reference config and mapped by its body pose. Disc A of joint k: a flat disc of radius rho centred on cA_k at radius F_k, normal cA_k, on the proximal body. Disc B: the same on cB_k, on the distal body (the two touch on the contact line). Sample each disc's skin face on a 2 mm grid; its 4.5 mm height is for collisions. Strap attachment: straps leave each disc on the side away from its partner, so at psi = 0 the two links of a joint are collinear through the pair. Body 1 is a 14 mm strap from disc B of J1 to disc A of J2 along the great-circle arc; body 2 likewise from J2B to J3A; body 3 is disc B of J3 plus the baseline's neck to BOTTOM (or drop the neck in both models). Heights: each disc face and each strap profile r(u) is fitted as the max over taken poses of (skin radius along the sample's posed direction + 2 mm), by ray cast on B.skin(i) or bisection on B.dist. Not taken (None) if: no IK; any metal B.dist < 0; or the orbiting disc B hits its partner's strap, i.e. in the proximal disc's tangent plane the angle between the strap's leaving direction and the direction to disc B's centre falls below 95 deg. Control: the same script with O20 v5 hubs (stack 12.25) on m_k instead of disc pairs, which is the baseline model. Report B.report() for both and the share of poses lost to the disc-strap rule.
sweep_params: Disc radius rho 5-10 mm. Pair orientation n_k about m_k, per joint, 0-180 deg. Rolling ratio: equal cones vs unequal (0.7-1.4). psi_max 70-95 deg. Disc height 4-6 mm. Base chains as for the 3R seeds (final, r20 s1414 #4).
prior_art: CORE compliant rolling-contact elements (Cannon, Lusk and Howell, ASME IDETC 2005) and the Rolamite (Wilkes, Sandia, 1967). Rolling-contact joints are used in robotic and prosthetic fingers and in knee designs. No conical-CORE shoulder exoskeleton is known to me.

name: 2R shoulder + self-stowing conformal humeral tape
topology: Scapula base -> J1: R hub, ACTIVE (axis b, hub-able: the lateral acromion edge) -> link 1 -> J2: R hub, ACTIVE (axis p2, arc a1 from b) -> link 2, which carries the humerus long axis at arc a2 from p2 (a 2R pointing chain) -> a link-2 carriage mount at station z down the arm -> a PASSIVE radial slide P (toward the humerus axis) and a PASSIVE yaw pivot R (axis parallel to the humerus axis) -> the carriage, with 4 MR52 guide rollers and 1 encoder roller pinching the tape -> humeral rotation phi, ACTIVE. The carriage runs along a pre-shaped superelastic NiTi tape (0.35 x 18 mm, 15 mm transverse curvature). One tape end is anchored to the upper-arm cuff region (the BOTTOM side); the tape lies arm-fixed 2-3 mm over the arm skin, in the plane perpendicular to the humerus at station z. Behind the carriage the tape winds onto an O14 constant-force spool on the carriage (PASSIVE, angle set by phi). There is no arm-end hub and no neck.
dof_reasoning: J1 and J2 point the humerus axis (2 DOF, axes through GH). The third DOF is the arm's spin about its own axis relative to link 2, which is the carriage's position along the arm-fixed tape: one coordinate, read by the encoder roller and driven in MVP2. The tape follows the non-round arm, so the carriage moves in and out and turns as it travels. The radial slide and the yaw pivot take exactly that, as functions of phi fixed by the tape's shape (closure). Tape + slide + pivot is geometrically equivalent to a pure rotation about the humerus axis, so the loop has mobility 3. The spool angle is set by the deployed length, and a constant-force spring keeps the tape wound. Nothing can sag: every passive coordinate is fixed by phi.
description: Two O20 hubs. J1 is scapula-fixed on the lateral acromion edge. Link 1 is a ~90 deg strap to J2, which sits over the posterior shoulder when the arm hangs. Link 2 runs from J2 down the posterior-lateral deltoid to a 22 x 20 x 7 mm carriage about 100 mm below GH. An 18 mm NiTi tape lies 2-3 mm over the arm skin, wrapped part-way round the arm inside the body-free window (theta -20..+62 deg about the humerus; 0 = lateral, + = posterior; FINDINGS), from its anchor to the carriage, and then into an O14 spool. Rest: the carriage is lateral and the tape covers only the arc between anchor and carriage. External rotation: the carriage moves toward the anchor and the tape winds in. Internal rotation / behind-back (Reach back pocket): the carriage runs to the far end of the window and the tape pays out behind it, but no tape exists beyond the carriage on the trunk side. Overhead: the 2R points link 2 up along the lateral arm; the tape is unchanged relative to the arm, and J1/J2 sit on top of the shoulder. Across-body: link 2 lies over the posterior deltoid and the carriage is near mid-window.
why_better: It removes the arm-end hub and neck. That zone costs 17 points of R1 (BOTTOM's hub sits on 23 mm of skin motion), and every part collision of the r20 picks over the workspace is 'link 2 - neck'. The humeral DOF moves farther down the arm, as the user suggested, onto a track that hugs the non-round arm: a circular ring sees 13.5-25 mm of skin-radius spread at every station 80-280 mm down the arm. The track exists only between its anchor and the carriage, so the narrow body-free window is used only as far as each pose needs. The 2R pointing singularity has a home: a singular margin of 18.6 deg over the whole bench workspace with a hub-able J1 at bvec(100,20), or 26.7 deg if J1's axis may point into the back (computed here on the bench's 470 poses).
main_risk: The deployed tape is a curved cantilever between anchor and carriage, and carriage loads bend and twist it. MVP1's <= 5 N at the cuff is probably fine; MVP2 needs a Bi-STEM pair or a rigid telescoping arc. The tape is fixed in the humerus frame, so it stands off where the deltoid or triceps bulge. The 2R's singular margin (19-27 deg) means fast J1 rates near it. The 67-87 deg of humeral travel, plus carriage and spool, must fit the -20..+62 deg window. NiTi spool fatigue. Joint technology: the humeral DOF is a tape-and-roller track, not a bearing joint, so it needs the user's acceptance.
unpowered_and_mvp2: MVP1: J1 and J2 on the v5 rolling pairs; the carriage on rollers. The constant-force spool spring (~2 N) biases humeral rotation by ~0.1 N.m, under R17's 1 N.m; a second, opposed spool on the anchor side can cancel it. No coordinate is free. Sensing: encoders on J1 and J2, plus the encoder roller (or the spool angle) for phi. MVP2: J1 and J2 as today (rim drums, remote motors); humeral rotation by a Bowden push-pull pair on the carriage along the tape, or a capstan on the encoder roller.
model_spec: Bench: B = CB.Bench(); Q_i = Rs.T @ Rh; scapula coords mapped to thorax by Rs; bvec, w_dir and circ_int from band_impl.py (numpy port). 2R: b = bvec(100, 20) (hub-able default; sweep it), a1 = a2 = 90 deg, branch +-1. Humerus axis h_i = Q_i @ [0,-1,0]; p2 = circ_int(b, a1, h_i, a2, branch) (for 90/90: p2 = branch * unit(b x h_i)). Return None if angle(b, h_i) < 15 or > 165 deg. Link 2 frame L2 = [h_i, e2, e3] with e2 = unit(p2 - (p2.h_i) h_i) and e3 = h_i x e2. Arm spin phi_i = the signed angle about h_i from e2 to the projection of Q_i @ [0,0,1] (the humerus-frame lateral). A link-2-fixed direction at angle theta_c in L2 sits at humerus-frame angle theta = theta_c - phi_i (theta 0 = lateral +z, + toward posterior -x; check the sign once on a test pose). Tape (arm-fixed, humerus frame): station z (default 100 mm along -y); profile r_t(theta) for theta in [theta_a, theta_a + Theta] (default anchor theta_a = 62 deg at the posterior end, extending anteriorly to -20 deg); r_t(theta) = max over taken poses of the arm skin radius at (z, theta) + 2 mm + 0.35 mm. Arm skin radius: the first hit of the ray from Rh @ [0,-z,0] in direction Rh @ [-sin(theta), 0, cos(theta)] on B.skin(i); ignore hits beyond 120 mm. Carriage: theta_car,i = theta_c - phi_i, with theta_c chosen so that mid-range phi puts the carriage at the window centre. Taken only if theta_car stays within [-20 + 8, 62 - 8] deg (8 deg = half carriage) and the needed tape length is between 0 and Theta. Metal per pose (built in the humerus frame, mapped by Rh): tape samples for theta between theta_car,i and theta_a only, 18 mm wide along the arm (z +-9), every 2 mm, at r_t(theta); the carriage as a 22 (along the tape) x 20 (along the arm) x 7 mm box with its underside at r_t(theta_car) + 0.4; the spool as an O18 x 20 mm cylinder at r_t + 9 beside the carriage, on the side away from the anchor. The slide mount on link 2 is a fixed L2 point at radius R_m = max r_t + 9 and angle theta_c. The slide travel R_m - r_t(theta_car) - 9 must be within 0..12 mm, else not taken. Hubs: J1 disc on b at radius F1 and J2 disc on p2 at F2 (O20 v5, as the baseline). Link 1 is a 14 mm strap b -> p2. Link 2 is a 14 mm strap from p2 to the slide mount, with directions slerped from p2 to the mount's direction. All radius profiles are fitted as the max over taken poses of (skin radius along their posed sample directions + 2 mm). All metal is checked with B.dist (< 0 -> not taken). Report B.report(), the phi range used, and the share of poses lost to the window vs to skin contact.
sweep_params: J1 axis b over the hub-able region (singular-margin map: bvec(100,20) gives 18.6 deg); arcs a1, a2 70-110 deg plus branch; tape station z 70-150 mm; anchor angle theta_a and carriage angle theta_c within the -20..+62 deg window; clearance 2-3 mm. Realisation: conformal tape vs a 2-stage telescoping circular arc (rigid, stiffer, constant radius).
prior_art: Tape-spring / STEM and Bi-STEM deployable booms (spacecraft booms and antennas since the 1960s). Open semicircular humeral-rotation bearings in arm exoskeletons such as ARMin (Nef, Riener et al.). The 2R + humeral-ring split is this repo's P0 family (docs/P0_BASE_MOUNT.md, FINDINGS).

name: Geodesic strap gimbal: J2 as a self-stowing strap between two hubs
topology: Scapula base -> J1: R hub, ACTIVE (axis b through GH, on the acromion top) -> link 1 = J1's rotor + the deployed part of a strap lying on the great circle G perpendicular to p2 = unit(b x W_S). The strap is anchored at the J1 rotor, so it is link-1-fixed -> J2, ACTIVE: the strap's extension s = angle(b, W_S). Link 2's guide block (rollers pinching the strap, one encoder roller) slides along the strap, which is a rotation about p2 -> link 2 = the guide block + a spool (the strap tail winds onto an O16 constant-force spool) + a short arm to the J3 rotor -> J3: R hub, ACTIVE (axis W through GH, on the anterolateral deltoid; its lower member is BOTTOM's arm end). Passive: the spool angle (set by s) and the guide block's radial slide (set by the strap's radial profile). a1 = a2 = 90 deg (a gimbal). Generalisation: a1 = a2 = gamma < 90 deg puts the strap on the small circle of angular radius gamma about p2. Realisation: a Bi-STEM pair of superelastic NiTi tapes (0.3 x 20 mm), or a 2-3 stage band-synchronised telescoping Ti arc.
dof_reasoning: This is a spherical 3R with a1 = a2 = 90 deg (a gimbal). J1 and J3 are ordinary hubs. J2's axis p2 is perpendicular to both b and W, so every point of link 2 that lies on G moves along G when J2 turns. J2 is therefore realised as sliding along a strap that lies on G; its coordinate is the strap extension (encoder roller in MVP1, spool drive in MVP2). The spool angle follows the extension (a constant-force spring keeps it wound), and the guide block's radial slide follows the strap's fixed radial profile (closure). Exactly 3 coordinates, nothing free.
description: Only two hubs: J1 on the acromion top (scapula) and J3 on the anterolateral deltoid (arm). They are joined by one 20 mm strap that always runs the shortest way between them over the shoulder, 2-5 mm above the skin. There is no third hub and no link elbow. Over the bench workspace the hub separation is 23-157 deg (39-135 deg on the clips) for the default pair b = bvec(70,35), W = w_dir(55,30), which has a 22.5 deg singular margin (computed here on the 470 bench poses). Rest (arm hanging): the hubs are ~85-90 deg apart and the strap runs from the acromion over the lateral shoulder down to the deltoid. Abduction 90 deg: about 40 deg apart. Overhead: the hubs come within ~25-35 deg of each other over the top of the shoulder; the strap is short and its tail is wound in the spool beside J3. Across-body: the hubs separate and the strap is long over the front of the shoulder. Behind-back: the strap lies over the posterior shoulder. The strap's radius profile is link-1-fixed (fitted); the guide block on link 2 rides it up and down on its slide.
why_better: It attacks the two worst zones at once. The J2 hub zone (18 points of R1, unfixable by shape) does not exist. Link 2 no longer detours through an off-path J2 (the final's J2 lands on the back over the medial scapula at 142-150 deg). The metal is the shortest path between two hubs, each of which can sit on low-motion skin. The links fully overlap, as the user hinted, so they cannot collide with each other. The strap meets J3 tangentially in its own plane, so no neck bridges a link, which removes R16's 'link 2 - neck' collisions. One strap plus a spool is light.
main_risk: Gimbal lock: with hub-able axes the best singular margin found over the bench workspace is only ~20-22 deg (the strap must cover 23-157 deg). Near that margin J1 and J3 spin fast and an unpowered chain can hesitate. The deployed strap is a curved cantilever up to ~150 mm long; it needs Bi-STEM or telescoping stages, and twisting under load misaligns J3. The strap's radius profile is fixed in link 1's frame, so where the skin under the geodesic changes with the arm (the deltoid end) it must stand off. The spool and guide block (~20 x 20 x 9 mm) beside J3 add a lump on the deltoid. Joint technology: J2 is a strap-and-roller slide, not a bearing joint, so it needs the user's acceptance.
unpowered_and_mvp2: MVP1: J1 and J3 on v5 rolling pairs; the guide block on 4 rollers. The spool's constant-force spring (~2 N) biases J2 by ~0.14 N.m (R17 limit: 1 N.m); a second spool on link 1 can cancel it. Sensing: J1 and J3 encoders, plus the guide's encoder roller (or the spool angle) for J2. MVP2: J1 and J3 rim drums as today; J2 driven at the spool (a remote cable on a drum on the spool shaft, with the spring returning it) or by a push-pull cable on the guide block. The stiffness of the deployed strap is the open MVP2 question.
model_spec: Bench: B = CB.Bench(); Q_i = Rs.T @ Rh; scapula coords mapped to thorax by Rs; bvec and w_dir from band_impl.py. Axes: b = bvec(70, 35), W0 = w_dir(55, 30); this is the best hub-able pair found (margin 22.5 deg). Also try b(65,40) / W(55,20) (22.4 deg) and b(345,20) / W(80,-60) (20.3 deg). gamma = 90 deg. Per pose: p3 = Q_i @ W0; theta_i = angle(b, p3); return None if theta_i < 20 or > 160 deg. p2 = sigma * unit(b x p3), with sigma = +1 fixed. G_i is the great circle through b and p3. Strap station s (deg, measured from b toward p3): u(s) = cos(s) b + sin(s) t, with t = unit(p3 - (p3.b) b). Strap stations are link-1-fixed (link-1 frame (b, p2, b x p2)), so the strap profile is a single function r_S(s), s in [0, 160]. Link 2: the guide block sits at s_g,i = theta_i - s_c, with s_c = 20 deg by default (a link-2-fixed offset from J3 along G). The spool lies between the guide and J3 (centre at theta_i - s_c/2; a cylinder O18 x 22 with its axis along p2), and an arm connects the spool to the J3 rotor. Metal per pose: J1 hub disc on b at radius F1; J3 hub (O20 v5, lower plate on the arm) on p3 at F3; strap samples on G_i for s from 7 deg (the J1 rotor rim) to s_g,i, 20 mm wide (+-10 mm along p2), every 2 mm, at radius r_S(s); the guide block, 24 x 24 x 9 mm, centred at s_g,i with its underside at r_S(s_g,i) + 0.5; the spool and arm on link 2 at fixed link-2 coordinates (radius fitted). Strap profile fit: r_S(s) = max over taken poses with s <= s_g,i of (skin radius along u(s) and +-10 mm across + 2 mm), by ray cast from GH on B.skin(i) or bisection with B.dist. Guide slide: the block's mount on link 2 sits at radius M = max r_S + 9. The slide travel M - r_S(s_g,i) - 9 must be within 0..14 mm, else not taken. Hub faces F1 and F3 are fitted as the max need. Not taken if theta is outside [20, 160], the slide travel is out of range, or any metal has B.dist < 0. Telescoping variant: the strap is two Ti arcs at constant radii R and R + 3. Stage A is link-1-fixed from b with length L_A; stage B is link-2-fixed, running back from p3, with length L_B; L_A + L_B = 160 + 20 deg of overlap. Include the stages' overhangs past the far hub as metal, and report both variants. gamma < 90 variant: p2 = circ_int(b, gamma, p3, gamma, sigma), with the strap on the small circle of angular radius gamma about p2. Report B.report(), the theta range used, and the poses lost to the singular margin vs to skin.
sweep_params: (b, W) pair from the singular-margin map; top hub-able pairs: b(70,35) / W(55,30) 22.5 deg, b(65,40) / W(55,20) 22.4 deg, b(345,20) / W(80,-60) 20.3 deg. gamma 75-90 deg. Spool offset s_c 12-30 deg. Strap width 14-20 mm. Realisation: Bi-STEM tape vs 2-3 stage telescoping arcs. J1 and J3 hub radii.
prior_art: Gimbals (90/90 spherical 3R); curved remote-centre guides in surgical robots; Bi-STEM booms. I know of nothing with the middle joint realised as a deployable strap. It matches the user's 2026-10-14 hint that the joints 'fully overlap each other'.

name: Hubless chain on magnet-preloaded open ball races
topology: Scapula base -> J1, ACTIVE arc joint: a Ti race plate (12 mm wide, 2.5 mm thick, 90 deg gothic groove, 0.5 mm 17-4PH strip in its floor) lies on the cone of angular radius gamma1 about axis b, spanning J1's travel, on the proximal or distal member. The other member's 25 mm carriage rides it on 8 caged O2 Si3N4 balls, held down by 4 O3 x 1.5 N52 magnets; the race has no lips -> link 1 (strap) -> J2, ACTIVE arc joint: a race and carriage on the cone of radius gamma2 about p2 -> link 2 -> J3, ACTIVE arc joint: a race and carriage on the cone of radius gamma3 about W, with the arm-end member on BOTTOM. W may be the humerus axis, in which case the race is the humeral ring. No hub sits at any axis pierce point, and axes may point where no hub could sit (into the back or neck, down the arm). Gamma can exceed 90 deg, which puts the race around the other end of the axis line.
dof_reasoning: The kinematics are those of a spherical 3R (three revolutes with axes through GH), realised as arcs: each carriage's position along its race is the joint angle. The balls are rolling elements and the magnets a preload; neither adds a coordinate. Exactly 3.
description: Flat: every joint is a 7 mm stack of curved plates (race 2.5 + balls 2 + carriage 2.5) on a small circle around its axis; there are no hubs and no caps. Rest: J1's race arcs over the posterior-superior scapula (base-fixed, low-motion skin) around an axis that may point into the back or neck. Link 1 runs from its carriage over the top of the shoulder to J2's race. J3's race wraps part-way round the upper arm at deltoid level if W is the humerus axis (the humeral ring), or circles a spot on the deltoid otherwise. Overhead: the carriages sit at the ends of their races, which stay put on their own members, while the axis pierce points (acromion tip, humeral head) carry no metal. Across-body and behind-back: J3's arm-fixed race turns with the arm while the link-2 carriage stays with link 2, and an open race can stop short of the trunk-contact side.
why_better: It decouples where a joint's metal sits from where its axis points. A hub chain must put a hub at each axis's pierce point, which confines the axes to hub-able skin. Computed here on the bench's 470 poses: the 2R pointing singular margin is 26.7 deg only if J1's axis points into the back, and 18.6 deg with a hub-able axis; for the gimbal it is 32 vs 22.5 deg. Joints become 7 mm instead of 12.25 mm, can be routed over low-motion skin (base 82-98 % in band), and leave high-relief pierce points bare. Open races (no lips) are thinner, can end anywhere, and break away in a collision instead of pinching (safety).
main_risk: Each race spans its joint's whole travel. J1's travel is ~190-220 deg over the workspace: at gamma 25 deg and R 70 mm that is ~120 mm of plate per joint, more metal sweeping over moving skin than a hub, especially J2's race on link 1. The magnetic preload (~12 N) holds MVP1 loads only; MVP2 needs lips or a wire race (+2-3 mm). Open races collect debris (the shoulder-pad cover helps). It is a custom bearing, not a catalogue part, so the user should agree to it as MVP1's 'basic rolling bearing'.
unpowered_and_mvp2: MVP1: balls in a ground groove; rolling friction ~0.005 x preload gives a negligible torque. Nothing is free. Sensing: a magnetic linear scale on each race, read by the carriage (the user's choice). MVP2: one push-pull cable pair per joint in the race groove, with the Bowden ends at the race ends (a curved linear drive); lips or a wire-race carriage for 10 N.m.
model_spec: Bench: B = CB.Bench(); Q_i = Rs.T @ Rh; scapula coords mapped to thorax by Rs; bvec, w_dir, circ_int and tri_ok from band_impl.py (numpy port). Kinematics: the spherical 3R closed form (p1 = b; p3 = Q_i @ W0; p2 = circ_int(b, a1, p3, a2, branch)). Axis seeds: (1) the final, b = bvec(32.55,80.56), W0 = w_dir(71.38,4.78), a = 77.41 / 81.45, branch -1; (2) 2R + ring, b = bvec(295,-35) (margin 26.7 deg), W0 = [0,-1,0] (the humerus axis), a1 = a2 = 90; (3) free directions (sweep). Joint angles from the closed form: q1 = the pin angle about b as in band_impl (e = unit(b x y), f = b x e); q2 = the signed angle at p2 between the arcs to p1 and p3; q3 = the spin about p3 of a humerus-fixed reference relative to p2. Over the taken bench poses compute each joint's range [qmin, qmax]. Race k sits on member A (default: proximal) as an arc of the circle at angular radius gamma_k about the axis m_k, in A's frame, from azimuth phi_k + qmin - 8 deg to phi_k + qmax + 8 deg (8 deg = half a carriage at R 70). The carriage on member B is a 25 mm arc at B-fixed azimuth phi_k on the same circle (so it sits at phi_k + q in A's frame). Sample race and carriage undersides every 2 mm along the arc x 3 across the 12 mm width. The race underside radius r_race(az) is an A-fixed profile, fitted as the max over taken poses of (skin radius + 2 mm) along the posed sample directions. The carriage rides 2.5 mm above the race plate (total stack 7 mm); sample only its exposed underside. Links: member 1 connects its J1 carriage to its J2 race (a 14 mm strap along the shortest arc between their nearest points, radius fitted); member 2 connects its J2 carriage to its J3 race or carriage; the arm-end member carries J3's race (or carriage) and BOTTOM's neck as in the baseline. A pose is not taken if the chain does not close, a carriage leaves its race (possible only for a trimmed race), or any metal has B.dist < 0.
sweep_params: Per joint: gamma_k 15-165 deg (either end of the axis line), carriage azimuth phi_k, race on the proximal or distal member. Race trimmed to the clip range (accepting lost workspace poses) vs the full workspace range. Axis seeds: baseline; 2R + ring with J1 into the back (bvec(295,-35)); free directions. Stack 6-8 mm.
prior_art: Thin-section four-point and wire-race bearings (Kaydon, Franke; see docs/research/ring_and_shell_hardware.md); magnetically preloaded linear stages; curved remote-centre guides in surgical robots; the Rolamite (Wilkes 1967), an alternative low-stack rolling guide.

name: Cam-unfolding link: a slaved flexure knee in link 2
topology: Scapula base -> J1: R hub, ACTIVE (b) -> link 1 -> J2: R hub, ACTIVE (p2), with an O28 x 3 mm groove face cam on link 1 around the J2 hub -> link 2a (MR52 follower on a lever, O2 Ti pushrod along 2a) -> J4: PASSIVE cross-spring flexure pivot (two crossed 0.4 x 6 mm Ti leaves standing radially; axis p4 through GH; +-18 deg). Its angle is slaved, q4 = c(q2), by the cam through the pushrod and a 6 mm crank on 2b -> link 2b -> J3: R hub, ACTIVE (W, the arm end on BOTTOM). Variant: a spherical four-bar coupler between link 1 and link 2b instead of the cam.
dof_reasoning: A spherical 4R whose fourth joint is not free: its angle is a fixed function of q2, imposed by a groove cam (closure, positive drive). The chain therefore has 3 coordinates, and the 3 hub encoders give the arm's orientation through the known c(q2). The 4R designs failed R17 because their spare joint fell within 0.1 s; here J4 cannot move unless J2 moves.
description: It looks like the baseline 3R with a thin 'knee' in the middle of link 2 (a crossed-flexure pivot, 6 mm tall, no bearing stack) and a small cam ring around J2. Arm hanging: the knee folds link 2, so its effective arc a2 is short and J2 sits closer to J3, lower on the side of the shoulder. Overhead: J2 has turned far and the cam opens the knee, so link 2 lengthens and J2 is held up over the top of the shoulder instead of sinking onto the medial scapula. Across-body and behind-back: c(q2) chooses the arc that keeps link 2 out of the arm-trunk gap (the squeeze that cost Reach back pocket).
why_better: It adds a designable function c(q2) to the 3R without a spare coordinate. The effective arc a2(q2) can shorten where J2 would otherwise ride high-relief skin and lengthen overhead, and the 3R's fold singularities (a fixed-arc spherical triangle) can be moved out of the range: what a 4R offers, without R17's sag. The compact designs lose most of their workspace to shape and squeeze (FINDINGS), and the proximity agent concluded that R1 >= 90 % needs 'a different joint path, not better parts'. A pose-dependent link geometry changes the path.
main_risk: The cam and pushrod sit in link 2b's load path: MVP2's 10 N.m needs a stout cam or a four-bar coupler instead. A single c(q2) may help some poses and hurt others. The flexure's +-18 deg limits how far the path can change. The IK of the coupled chain can have two roots (branch jumps). The extra parts at J2 (cam ring, follower) add a lump exactly where R1 already loses most.
unpowered_and_mvp2: MVP1: hubs on v5 rolling pairs; the follower bearing runs in a groove cam. The flexure's stiffness (~0.2 N.m at 18 deg), reflected to J2 through the cam slope, stays under 0.15 N.m, well within R17. MVP2: three remote-motor hubs as today; J4 stays passive. Sensing: encoders on J1-J3.
model_spec: Bench: B = CB.Bench(); Q_i = Rs.T @ Rh; scapula coords mapped to thorax by Rs; bvec, w_dir and circ_int from band_impl.py. Product-of-exponentials model at a reference pose i0 (the bench pose with the smallest elevation), starting from the final's chain: b = bvec(32.55,80.56), W0 = w_dir(71.38,4.78), a = 77.41 / 81.45 deg, branch -1, Q0 = Q_i0. Axes in the reference config: m1 = b; m2 = p2(i0); m4 = slerp(p2(i0), p3(i0), f) with f = 0.5 by default; m3 = p3(i0). The chain R(q1,q2,q3) = Rot(m1,q1) Rot(m2,q2) Rot(m4,c(q2)) Rot(m3,q3) Q0 must equal Q_i, with q measured from the reference. IK: scipy least_squares on the rotation-vector residual. Seeds: the baseline closed-form q (c ~ 0) and a 4-seed grid. Accept if the residual is < 1e-6 and |c| <= 18 deg. c(q2): a cubic spline through 5 knots spread over the baseline's q2 range (knot values swept in [-18, 18] deg), with |dc/dq2| <= 0.6. c = 0 must reproduce the baseline. Body poses: link 1 = Rot(m1,q1); link 2a = link1 Rot(m2,q2); link 2b = link2a Rot(m4,c(q2)); arm = link2b Rot(m3,q3). Metal is defined in the reference config and mapped by body pose: hubs J1 (base lower plate), J2 and J3 as O20 v5 discs (skin faces sampled; 12.25 mm stack for collisions); J4 as a flexure block with a 12 x 12 mm footprint, 6 mm tall, half on 2a and half on 2b; the cam ring as an annulus r 10-14 mm around J2 on link 1, 3 mm tall; links 1, 2a and 2b as 14 mm straps along the great-circle arcs between their joints. All radius profiles are fitted as the max over taken poses of (skin radius + 2 mm) along the posed sample directions. Not taken if there is no IK, c is out of range, or any metal has B.dist < 0. Report B.report(), the range of the effective arc a2_eff = angle(p2, p3), and the singular margin (angle(p1, p3) against a1 +- a2_eff).
sweep_params: J4 position f 0.3-0.7 along link 2; c(q2): 5 spline knots in [-18, 18] deg with slope <= 0.6; flexure range 12-20 deg; base chains (final, r20 s1414 #4) as seeds. Variant: c driven by q3 through a cam at J3, or J4 placed in link 1 with c(q1).
prior_art: Redundant spherical chains with coupled joints, usually coupled by gears or belts; variable-geometry linkages with cam-coupled joints. I know of none in shoulder exoskeletons.

name: Non-concurrent 3R on a compliant translation cuff stage
topology: Scapula base -> J1: R hub, ACTIVE; its axis line passes through a point c1 (not GH), in a direction near the local scapula skin normal -> link 1 -> J2: R hub, ACTIVE, axis line through c2 -> link 2 -> J3: R hub, ACTIVE, on a 'floating arm-end' block, with its axis near the local arm skin normal at a low-motion spot -> floating block -> a PASSIVE compliant 3-translation stage: along-arm P (+-12 mm) and around-arm P (+-8 mm) as two Ti parallel-leaf flexures (0.5 x 10 x 60 mm leaves), plus radial P (+-4 mm) as a thin leaf pair -> BOTTOM / the upper-arm cuff (the user's).
dof_reasoning: Three revolutes whose directions give the arm's orientation, with the same direction kinematics as a spherical 3R. Because the axis lines do not meet at GH, the chain's end is off by a translation e(q), which the three passive stage translations take up. These are the user-approved passive self-aligning slides at the cuff, outside the count: they are never powered or measured, and orientation sensing uses only the 3 encoders. Loop mobility: chain 3 + stage 3 + GH 3 - 6 = 3, so every coordinate is set by the arm. The stage's centring stiffness (<= 0.4 N/mm) keeps it from flopping and bounds the cuff force (R17: <= 5 N).
description: Three hubs, each seated flat on its own skin, perpendicular to the local skin normal at a low-motion spot. J1 is on the scapula's acromion/spine. J3 is on the deltoid near W ~ (112, -15) deg, where the proximity agent found a 94 % flat-disc ceiling. The two straps joining them are not constrained to a sphere about GH. Under BOTTOM, a 60 x 40 mm Ti leaf-spring stage lets the arm-end block shift relative to the cuff. Rest: the stage is centred (the chain is assembled at rest). Overhead and across-body: the stage deflects by the chain's own translation error, up to its +-12 / 8 / 4 mm limits, and on a real body also by the GH translation the bench does not model. Behind-back: the same.
why_better: 'All axes through GH' is what tilts hubs on the flat back and on the arm (whose skin normal points away from the humerus axis, not from GH), and what ties every link to a sphere about GH. Dropping that constraint lets each hub sit flat on low-motion skin. It is also the only concept here that absorbs real GH translation (R10's 4 mm, and the literature's up to 35 mm superior at 90 deg scaption) instead of being misaligned by it, a benefit the bench cannot show because the rig's GH is fixed.
main_risk: The stage travel is finite. The design's own offsets (|e| up to ~1.8x the offset) plus real GH translation must fit within +-12 / 8 / 4 mm, which limits axis offsets to ~5 mm and the bench gain to the few points that flat hubs buy. A 3-axis stage adds metal and mass at the cuff. On the bench (no GH translation) it may well look worse than the baseline; its real case is R10/R14.
unpowered_and_mvp2: MVP1: hubs on v5 rolling pairs; the stage leaves are elastic (<= 0.4 N/mm, <= 5 N at full travel). Nothing is free. MVP2: hubs driven as today. The stage passes moments (all translations are free), so the assist reaches the arm as a pure moment through the cuff.
model_spec: Bench: B = CB.Bench(); per pose (Rs, Rh) from B.frames(i); scapula coords mapped to thorax by Rs; bvec, w_dir and circ_int from band_impl.py. Work with rigid transforms (R, t), not rotations only. Directions as the final (b = bvec(32.55,80.56) in S; p2 by circ_int with a = 77.41 / 81.45, branch -1; W0 = w_dir(71.38,4.78) in H), so the orientation IK stays closed-form (q1, q2, q3). If directions are tilted by up to 20 deg, re-solve the orientation IK with least_squares on the rotation-vector residual. Axis lines: J1 through c1 (scapula-fixed), J2 through c2 (link-1/link-2-fixed), J3 through c3 (link-2/arm-end-fixed), with c_k = r_k m_k + o_k, o_k perpendicular to m_k and |o_k| <= 10 mm (o_k = 0 is the spherical baseline). FK as a product of exponentials with twists xi_k = (m_k, c_k x m_k) in the reference config (the bench pose with the smallest elevation, where the chain is assembled with zero stage offset): T_3 = exp(xi1 q1) exp(xi2 q2) exp(xi3 q3) T_ref. The translation error at pose i is e_i = t(T_3); expressed in the humerus frame, e_H = Rh^T e_i. Stage check: the along-arm component (along -y_H) must be within +-12 mm, around-arm (tangential at the block) +-8, and radial +-4, else not taken. Metal: O20 v5 hubs at c_k + F_k m_k (lower plates perpendicular to m_k). J1's direction is the scapula skin normal at its seat in the rest pose. J3's direction is the arm skin normal at W ~ (112, -15) deg, 60 mm from GH (humerus frame), if the orientation IK still closes. Straps run between hub rims; their radius profiles are fitted as the max over taken poses of (skin distance + 2 mm) along the posed directions. The floating block (the arm-end hub's lower plate plus a 60 x 40 x 6 mm stage under BOTTOM) sits at its humerus-fixed pose translated by e_i. Not taken if there is no IK, the stage limits are exceeded, or any metal has B.dist < 0. Report B.report(), the max |e| per component, and the same run with o_k = 0 as the control.
sweep_params: Axis offsets |o_k| 0-10 mm per joint; axis tilt from radial 0-20 deg; hub seat locations (J3 boxed near W (112, -15) deg); stage limits (along +-8..15, around +-5..10, radial +-3..5 mm); chain seeds (final, agD_n3_wbox_1).
prior_art: Passive DOFs to tolerate human-robot misalignment (Schiele and van der Helm, IEEE TNSRE 2006); self-aligning exoskeleton axes (Stienen et al., IEEE T-RO 2009); the user's own decision on passive self-aligning cuff slides (REQUIREMENTS.md).

name: Four-bar base: J2 carried along a synthesised coupler path
topology: Scapula base with two hubs, A0 (crank pivot, ACTIVE) and B0 (rocker pivot, PASSIVE), axes through GH, 25-40 mm apart on the acromion/spine -> a crank (arc alpha) and a rocker (arc beta) -> the coupler = link 1, whose joints A1 and B1 are PASSIVE with axes through GH (together, a spherical four-bar). The coupler carries J2's axis p2 at a coupler point -> J2: R hub, ACTIVE -> link 2 -> J3: R hub, ACTIVE, on BOTTOM's arm end. 6 joints, 3 active.
dof_reasoning: The spherical four-bar is a 1-DOF loop: the crank angle sets the rocker and both coupler joints (closure), so link 1's motion is one coordinate, measured and driven at the crank hub on the base. J2 and J3 are ordinary active revolutes. All axes pass through GH. That gives 3 active and 3 passive coordinates set by closure. The four-bar's dead points must stay outside the crank range so that nothing can toggle.
description: On the scapula sits a compact 'hand': two base hubs, a short crank and a short rocker holding link 1 at two points. Link 1 swings J2 not around a single base axis but along a synthesised coupler curve, for example one that keeps J2 over skin of nearly constant radius from GH (the circle about b crosses skin 58-93 mm from GH, which is the J2 zone's problem). Rest: J2 over the posterior-superior shoulder. Overhead: the coupler lifts and slides J2 over the top instead of carrying it down onto the medial scapula. Across-body: J2 swings anteriorly along the curve. Behind-back: J2 stays posterior-superior while link 2 reaches down the posterior arm. Link 2 and the arm hub are as in the baseline.
why_better: The J2 hub zone (18 points) is lost because J2's path, a circle about the base axis, crosses skin 58-93 mm from GH. A spherical four-bar's coupler curve has 8-10 parameters, enough to follow a ridge of constant relief, while the extra pivots sit on the scapula's low-motion skin (base 82-98 % in band). A base-mounted crank also gives the MVP2 motor its shortest cable.
main_risk: The coupler also rotates link 1 in a coupled way, so J2's axis direction along the path is not free and the reachable set changes (it may lose workspace). Two extra hubs on the base add metal near the acromion, where the raised arm meets the base tab. Four-bar dead points or branch changes may fall inside the range. More parts.
unpowered_and_mvp2: MVP1: all six joints on rolling bearings (v5 hubs; the two passive coupler joints can use smaller O14 bearings). No coordinate is free if the crank range avoids dead points (transmission angle > 25 deg). MVP2: motors at the base crank, J2 and J3 hubs.
model_spec: Bench: B = CB.Bench(); Q_i = Rs.T @ Rh; scapula coords mapped to thorax by Rs; bvec, w_dir and circ_int from band_impl.py (numpy port). Spherical four-bar in the scapula frame: base pivots A0 and B0 (unit vectors; seed A0 = the final's b = bvec(32.55,80.56), B0 = 30 deg from A0 toward the scapular spine), crank arc alpha (A0 -> A1), rocker arc beta (B0 -> B1), coupler arc c (A1 -> B1). Position for crank angle t: A1 = Rot(A0, t) A1_0; B1 = circ_int(B0, beta, A1, c, s4), where s4 is the assembly branch. Coupler frame: E = [A1, unit(B1 - (B1.A1) A1), their cross product]. J2's axis p2(t) = E @ k, with k the coupler point (2 params: its arc from A1 and its angle from the A1 -> B1 direction). Chain closure: p3 = Q_i @ W0 (W0 = w_dir(71.38,4.78)), which requires angle(p2(t), p3) = a2 (81.45 deg). Scan t over the crank range in 1 deg steps, find the sign changes of g(t) = acos(p2(t).p3) - a2, and refine by bisection. Choose the root nearest the previous clip frame's t (clip poses are in time order), or for workspace poses the root with the larger four-bar transmission angle. Reject if there is no root, the transmission angle is < 25 deg, or the J2 triangle (p2-related arcs to p1-side and p3) is within 10 deg of a fold. Bodies: crank (A0 -> A1 strap), rocker (B0 -> B1), coupler/link 1 (A1, B1, p2 hubs + straps), link 2 (p2 -> p3), arm-end hub at p3. Hubs: A0 and B0 as base-fixed O20 discs; A1 and B1 as O16 (smaller passive bearings); J2 and J3 as O20 v5; straps 12-14 mm. Each body's radius profile is fitted as the max over taken poses of (skin radius along the posed sample directions + 2 mm). Synthesis: optimise the 9 parameters (A0 and B0 on the scapula: 4; alpha, beta, c; k: 2) with CMA-ES, <= 300 evaluations, on a cheap proxy: the spread (p90 - p10) over the clip poses of the skin radius under p2, subject to closure in >= 95 % of clips. Then run the full bench. Report B.report() and the J2 skin-radius spread against the baseline's 58-93 mm.
sweep_params: Base pivots A0 and B0 on the scapula (4 params); crank, rocker and coupler arcs alpha, beta, c (20-60 deg); coupler point k (2 params); assembly branch; a2 and W of the distal 2R; crank range.
prior_art: Spherical four-bar synthesis (Chiang, Kinematics of Spherical Mechanisms, 1988). Coupler-driven (polycentric) joints are common in knee orthoses and prostheses; I know of none used as a shoulder-exoskeleton base joint.

name: Crossed muscle-line rails (scapula-fixed acromial arch crossed by an arm-fixed humeral-head collar)
topology: Spherical 3R with no strap links. Scapula base -> R1 = carriage 1 on a scapula-fixed circular arc rail (rail 1, the 'acromial arch': a small circle of half-angle a12 about axis a1 through GH, lying over the acromion / supraspinatus / spine) [ACTIVE] -> R2 = bearing between carriage 1 and carriage 2 on the radial axis a2 through the rails' crossing point (v5 O20 hub or a thin-section ring) [ACTIVE] -> R3 = carriage 2 on an arm-fixed circular arc rail (rail 2, the 'collar': a small circle of half-angle a23 about an arm-fixed axis a3, around the top of the humeral head just under the acromion edge; part of the arm piece that runs on to BOTTOM) [ACTIVE] -> arm. All three axes through GH. Passive in the chain: none (the user's torque-free cuff slides stay outside the count).
dof_reasoning: Exactly the three revolutes of a spherical 3R: J1 = carriage-1 position on rail 1 (rotation about a1), J2 = hub angle between the two carriages (about a2), J3 = carriage-2 position on rail 2 (rotation about a3). For a given arm orientation a2 is the intersection of two cones (a12 from a1 in the scapula frame, a23 from a3 in the arm frame) on a fixed branch, so all three coordinates are functions of the arm pose: the crossing point is unique, both carriages are captive on their rails, nothing can sag. All three must be sensed (MVP2 powered); none is spare. The only degeneracy is the 3R singularity, which here is visible as the two rails becoming tangent (crossing angle -> 0); the model keeps it >= 25 deg.
description: Two curved rails and one small double carriage, no links. Rail 1 (~10 x 5 mm Ti with a rolling-element track) is part of the exo-scapula: an arch over the top of the shoulder along the acromion / scapular spine, ~52-60 mm from the GH centre. That skin is the most stable of the shoulder in the scapula frame: 37-58 mm from GH both at rest and at 150 deg elevation (my lookup on the rig). Rail 2 is part of the arm piece: a collar arc around the top of the humeral head, ~20 deg above the arm's equator. This is the arm's low-motion band (delta 100-125; the proximity agent's best arm-fixed spot w(112,-15): point ceiling 99 %, disc ceiling 94 %). The collar carries on as the neck to BOTTOM. The rails cross at one point, where the double carriage holds the J2 bearing. Rest: the arch sits on the acromion, the collar's lateral arc lies under its lateral end over the deltoid cap, and they cross near the acromion's lateral edge. Overhead: the arm turns the collar up under the arch and the crossing slides along both rails. The arch stays clear because the scapula's upward rotation keeps the arm axis below the scapula's horizon: <= +5 deg in all 110 bench clip frames, and arch directions bvec(0..45, 60) stay >= 59 deg from the arm axis over the whole bench workspace (my check). Across-body: the crossing runs to the anterior end of the arch and the collar's posterior arc rises over the back of the head. Behind-back: the crossing runs to the posterior end (over the spine). The only metal that moves against both bodies is the ~30 mm double carriage. The upper rail sits one carriage stack (~12-16 mm) above the lower one.
why_better: It attacks the two largest R1 losses of the baseline (docs/research/proximity_levers.md), both of which are metal moving against both the scapula and the arm. (1) The J2 hub zone: 18.5 % of the covered skin at 0.7 % in band, and shape cannot fix it because J2 sweeps skin 58-93 mm from GH. (2) Link 2's ribbon: 16 points. Here each rail is fixed to the body whose skin it rides: the arch to the scapula (top / posterosuperior skin, 1.8-3.5 mm radial motion, ceiling 100 %) and the collar to the arm's best band. J2's swept path becomes body-fixed metal on stable skin instead of a hub flying over moving skin. No part has to clear the whole workspace against both bodies: the arch only has to clear the arm, and the collar only the trunk. Kinematics-only screen (my quick random search over the bench's 470 poses, no skin): some spherical 3R parameter sets keep J2 above 35 deg elevation in the scapula frame in 66-92 % of clip frames AND inside the arm cap band (delta 75-130) in 84-100 % of them. They close in 97-100 % of clip frames and 83-99 % of workspace poses at a crossing angle >= 25 deg (seeds in model_spec).
main_risk: (1) Stack at the crossing: the upper rail's skin face sits Delta ~12-16 mm above the lower one's (rail 5 + carriage plate 3 + bearing 5-7 + plate 1). The crossing visits the whole travel of both rails, so the upper rail is ~15-20 mm off the skin wherever it crosses: probably outside 10 mm, marginal at 14 mm. (2) Rail length: the same screen needs rail-1 travel of ~120-200 deg (115-160 mm) and rail-2 travel of ~65-150 deg (80-180 mm) on the fit clips, and more for the workspace. That costs mass and stiffness: open curved cantilevers twist ~2-5 deg per 75 mm under 25 N.m (docs/research/ring_and_shell_hardware.md). The rail ends become joint limits that cap reach. (3) A constant-radius rail over skin whose radius varies 37-58 mm along the arch loses band where the spread exceeds 12 mm (skin-cam-rails fixes this). (4) Short carriages can jam or bind under tilt (drawer effect) and near small crossing angles (R17 friction).
unpowered_and_mvp2: Unpowered: both carriages are captive on their rails and J2 is a plain rolling bearing, so the arm drives all three coordinates. Nothing sags because no coordinate is free. Rolling carriages (V-wheels or a caged-ball wire-race, ~10 mm stack per the hardware note) keep friction well under 1 N.m except near rail tangency, which is excluded. MVP2: J1 and J3 are circular rails about axes through GH, so a cable laid in a groove along each rail acts as a drum of radius rho*sin(a) ~50-65 mm (~150-200 N of cable tension for 10 N.m), pulling the carriage from both ends. J2 is a v5 hub with its own drum. Sensing: a magnetic arc scale along each rail read by its carriage (AS5311-type), and the v5 magnet / IC on J2.
model_spec: Conventions (band_impl / bench): bvec(az, el) is a scapula-frame direction (az 0 posterior, 90 lateral, 180 anterior, -90 medial; el up). w_dir(delta, az) is a canonical-humerus direction (delta from the distal humerus axis, az 0 lateral, +90 anterior). For pose i: scapula dir d -> S_R(i) @ d, with S_R = B.frames(i)['S'][0]. Arm dir d -> H_R(i) @ RH @ d, with H_R = B.frames(i)['H'][0] and RH = np.array(BP._rig().L['rest_humerus']) (H_R @ RH = rot(plane) rot(elev) rot(axial)). GH is the origin; a point = radius * unit direction. circ_int = a numpy port of band_impl.circ_int. PARAMS: a1 = bvec(az1, el1), a12, a3 = w_dir(d3, az3), a23, sigma (+-1), order ('arch_low' | 'collar_low'), Delta = 14 mm (upper skin face minus lower skin face), rail width 10 / thickness 5, carriage arc radius 13 mm, gamma_min 25 deg, Lmax 200 deg, rho_max 75 mm. SEEDS (az1, el1, a12, d3, az3, a23, sigma) from my kinematics-only screen: (64.9, 56.1, 57.4, 147.1, -119.0, 87.9, -1); (96.3, 31.3, 80.3, 148.0, -108.2, 87.9, -1); (119.5, 20.3, 86.6, 149.7, -45.0, 86.5, -1); (52.2, 37.4, 75.8, 62.6, 32.4, 70.3, +1). PASS 1 (all poses, no skin): A1 = S_R a1; A3 = H_R RH a3; (a2, ok) = circ_int(A1, a12, A3, a23, sigma). Crossing angle gamma = acos|t1.t3|, with t1 = unit(A1 x a2) and t3 = unit(A3 x a2). phi = angle of S_R^T a2 about a1 in a fixed basis (e1 = unit(a1 x h), e2 = a1 x e1, h = z unless |a1.z| > 0.9, then x). psi = the same for (H_R RH)^T a2 about a3. Centre each angle on its circular mean over the closing fit-clip frames and wrap to (-180, 180]. Extents: [min, max] over fit-clip frames with ok and gamma >= gamma_min, widened by the carriage half-length (13 / (rho sin a), rad -> deg) + 2 deg, then grown toward the workspace angles while length <= Lmax. HEIGHTS: rho_low = smallest radius (0.5 mm steps from 40) at which every skin-face sample of the lower rail is >= 2 mm from the skin (B.dist) in every fit-clip frame. rho_up = max(rho_low + Delta, the same rule applied to the upper rail). If part of a rail needs more than rho_max, trim its extent to the contiguous part under rho_max that contains the median angle. PASS 2 (per pose, then B.record): return None if not ok, gamma < gamma_min, phi or psi outside its extent shrunk by the carriage half-length, or any contact-only point has B.dist < 0. Skin-face samples on a 2 mm grid: rail 1 = scapula-frame dirs unit(cos(a12+b) a1 + sin(a12+b)(cos p e1 + sin p e2)) for p over its extent and b in +-5/rho, at its radius, mapped by S_R. Rail 2 = the same about a3 in the arm frame, mapped by H_R RH. Carriage = dirs within 13 mm of a2, at rho_low. Arm end = a 14 mm strip from the rail-2 end nearest BOTTOM, along the great circle to BOTTOM's cut end, radius ramped linearly from rho_2 to 96. BOTTOM's cut end is at canonical ~(0, -70, 67.5): band_impl's bar plane z0 67.5 along W (0, -0.071, 0.998), ~96 mm from GH; use the evaluator's neck p_bar if known. Contact-only points: rail tops (+5) and the J2 cap (dirs within 10 mm of a2, at rho_up + 6). VARIANT 'arch-and-strap': replace rail 2 with a 14 mm strap from the carriage (at rho_low + 3.15) to a v5 J3 hub at the arm spot w_dir(112, -15), whose lower member is an arm pad at its lowest legal radius. This variant has no crossing stack. REPORT: rail lengths (mm), gamma percentiles, and the share of poses lost to each test.
sweep_params: a1 (az 30-130, el 15-70); a12 (50-90); a3 in two families: collar (delta 130-155, az -130..-30) or lateral (delta 55-75, az 0-60); a23 (60-90); sigma; order (arch_low / collar_low); Delta (11-16 mm); Lmax (150-220 deg); gamma_min (20-30); the variant arch-and-strap on/off.
prior_art: Circular-arc remote-centre guides (surgical RCM arcs); semicircular humeral-rotation bearings in ARMin-type exos; MEDARM's curved girdle track; intersecting-circle (armillary) gimbals. I know of no exo that realises a spherical 3R as a scapula-fixed arch crossed by an arm-fixed collar with a double carriage at the crossing.

name: Skin-following cam rails with a telescoping crossing (profiled-radius version of the crossed rails)
topology: Same chain as crossed-muscle-rails, but the rails are not spheres. Scapula base -> R1 = carriage 1 on a scapula-fixed rail whose directions lie on the cone (a1, a12) and whose radius r1(phi) follows the scapula skin [ACTIVE] -> C2 = cylindrical joint on the radial axis a2 at the crossing: rotation [ACTIVE] + radial slide along a2 [PASSIVE, set by the two rail profiles] (rolling ball spline / linear ball bushing) -> R3 = carriage 2 on an arm-fixed rail on the cone (a3, a23) whose radius r2(psi) follows the arm skin; the rail continues down the lateral arm as the neck to BOTTOM [ACTIVE] -> arm.
dof_reasoning: A translation along an axis that passes through the GH centre does not change the orientation a spherical chain transmits. So each carriage may move radially as it travels without changing the 3R kinematics. Carriage 1 sits at r1(phi), set by rail 1's profile at its position; carriage 2 sits at r2(psi). Both phi and psi are functions of the arm pose (the 3R's two-cone closure), so the J2 slide length r2(psi) - r1(phi) is set by closure. That makes it a passive element driven by the chain, outside the active count (user rule 2026-10-15). It cannot sag because both carriages are captive on rails whose profiles fix it. Active: J1 (rail-1 position), J2 rotation, J3 (rail-2 position), which are the 3R's three coordinates.
description: The same picture as the crossed rails, but each rail is a 3-D curve that hugs its own skin. The exo-acromial arch dips to 2-4 mm over the acromion, where the skin is low (37-45 mm from GH), and rises over the supraspinatus / spine (55-60 mm). The arm collar follows the deltoid cap (45-64 mm across poses in the arm frame), then carries on down the lateral arm as the neck to BOTTOM, following the arm skin. At the crossing, a short ball-spline post on the J2 axis lets the two carriages sit at different heights: one carriage stack plus 0-15 mm of slide. Rest, overhead, across-body and behind-back: as in the crossed rails (the crossing travels along both rails). The difference is that the rails keep a constant clearance from their own skin instead of a constant radius, and the slide post grows where the arm rail's skin is higher than the arch's.
why_better: It removes the crossed rails' first weakness: a constant-radius rail over skin whose radius varies (37-58 mm along an arch over the top; 45-64 mm around the cap) loses band wherever the spread exceeds the 12 mm window. Here each rail's in-band ceiling is set only by the skin motion in its own frame (scapula top 1.8-3.5 mm; arm cap band ~12 mm), not by its shape. The proximity analysis classed 44 of the baseline's lost points as 'motion' that no reshaping on its path can recover. Profiled body-fixed rails turn most of that into slack that the profile can remove. The arm rail also doubles as the neck: the baseline's arm end + neck cover 34 % of the covered skin at 61 / 35 % in band, and here one part replaces three.
main_risk: (1) The slide post: where r2 - r1 at the crossing exceeds the carriage stack by more than 15-20 mm, J2 becomes a tall post. The upper rail's profile must then be raised to keep the slide short, which costs band. (2) The ball spline carries the J2 tilt moment (10 N.m in MVP2), which drives its section size and friction. (3) Non-circular rails need custom carriages that follow a varying radius and curvature (4 wheels on a 3-D curve). They are harder to make and to keep free of play, and need 5-axis machining. (4) All of the crossed rails' other risks remain (rail length, stack, tangency).
unpowered_and_mvp2: Unpowered: both carriages are captive and the slide is set by the profiles, so there is no free coordinate. Friction comes from two rail carriages and one ball spline (rolling, mu ~0.005). The slide's axial load is the radial component of the cuff force, which is small in MVP1 (< 5 N). MVP2: J1 and J3 are driven by cables. The cable cannot sit in a plain groove on a 3-D profiled rail, so use a closed channel, or a constant-radius drum sector fixed beside the rail, about the rail's own axis. J2 is driven by a v5 hub drum on the spline's outer sleeve. Sensing: arc scales on both rails and a magnet / IC on J2; the slide needs no sensing.
model_spec: Conventions as in crossed-muscle-rails: scapula dir -> S_R(i) d; arm dir (canonical, w_dir) -> H_R(i) @ RH @ d, with RH = BP._rig().L['rest_humerus']; GH origin; numpy band_impl.circ_int. KINEMATICS, extents, branch and None rules: exactly as crossed-muscle-rails pass 1 / pass 2 (same params a1, a12, a3, a23, sigma, gamma_min, Lmax and the same seeds). PROFILES: sample each rail every 2 deg along its extent x 3 across (b = 0, +-5 mm), giving body-frame directions d_k. Shaping poses = the bench's fit-clip poses + workspace poses (held-out clips are never in it). For each pose i, take the points r * R_i d_k for r = 30, 32, ..., 150 (R_i = S_R for rail 1, H_R RH for rail 2) and make one batched B.dist call per pose. r_exit(i, k) = the largest r with dist < 0 (0 if none). r_need(k) = max_i r_exit + 2.5. Rail directions with r_need > 85 are unusable: trim the extent to avoid them, and return None for poses that need them. r_low(s) = moving max of r_need over +-6 mm along the rail, then a smoothing spline with curvature radius >= 15 mm, + 0.5. Upper rail: r_up(psi) = max(its own smoothed r_need, max over closing poses with psi_i = psi of r_low(phi_i) + Delta_min), with Delta_min = 12, smoothed the same way. Slide stroke s_i = r_up(psi_i) - r_low(phi_i) - Delta_min; return None if s_i > stroke_max (15 mm). METAL per pose (skin faces, 2 mm grid): rail 1 at its profile along its directions, mapped by S_R; rail 2 at its profile, mapped by H_R RH; carriage = a disc of 13 mm arc radius around a2 at the lower rail's profile radius. Arm-rail neck: continue rail 2 beyond its travel end nearest BOTTOM, along the great circle, to BOTTOM's cut end (canonical ~(0, -70, 67.5)), profiled by the same r_need rule in the arm frame. Contact-only points: rail tops (+5), and the slide post as a 12 mm-radius cylinder along a2 from r_low to r_up + 6. Record the skin faces with B.record.
