name: Acromion gimbal + arm-fixed skin-shaped C-track (2 DOF at the shoulder, axial rotation lower on the arm)
topology: Scapula base -> J1: O20 hub, active R. Its axis a1 is fixed to the scapula and passes through GH; the hub sits on the lateral acromion top (default a1 = sdir(40,0)) -> L1 strap -> J2: O20 hub, active R. Its axis u2 passes through GH; this is an orthogonal gimbal by default (alpha12 = alpha23 = 90) -> L2: a short pointing yoke. Its frame follows the arm direction but not its axial rotation -> carriage, with a passive radial slide and a passive swivel about an axis parallel to the humeral axis -> rides an ARM-FIXED C-track at station s_t ~100 mm (deltoid insertion). The track is shaped to the arm's own skin at +4 mm and spans ~190 deg (anteromedial -> lateral -> posterolateral), open medially -> a track bracket merged into a shortened BOTTOM. Active joints: J1, J2, and the carriage's arc position on the track (the humeral rotation about the GH-elbow line). Passive: the radial slide and the swivel.
dof_reasoning: J1 and J2 point the humeral axis (2 DOF). The third active coordinate is where the carriage sits along the track, which equals the arm's rotation about its own GH-elbow axis relative to L2. It can be driven by a cable loop laid in the track groove and sensed by a magnetic strip. The track is non-circular because it follows the arm's skin, so the carriage needs a radial slide and a swivel. Both are fixed by the track geometry at every carriage position: they are set by closure, carry no load along their free direction, and cannot sag. Chain + arm therefore has exactly the arm's 3 DOF. Optional extra: let the carriage float +-8 mm along the arm (passive) so the arm end absorbs 2 of the 3 components of the real GH/handler translation.
description:
This is the user's own decomposition: two hubs form a clean gimbal at the shoulder, and humeral rotation gets its own joint lower on the arm. That joint is not a circular ring (a ring stands off a non-round arm: skin radius 38-73 mm around the humeral axis at s 90-120). It is an arm-fixed track that follows the arm's skin, so the long arc of the axial joint is arm-fixed metal over arm skin.
- Rest: J1 sits on the bony lateral acromion top (2-5 mm skin spread in the scapula frame). J2 is behind the humeral head at GH level (posterior branch). The short yoke runs down the posterolateral deltoid to the carriage on the lateral arm ~100 mm below GH. The track wraps from the biceps edge over the anterolateral strip (2-4 mm spread) and the posterolateral strip (0.7-1.6 mm) to the triceps edge.
- Overhead: the scapula-relative elevation peaks at ~128 deg, so the arm stays 10-25 deg (by a1 choice) from the gimbal poles. J2 swings to the posterior-superior side; track and yoke move with the arm. The J1 hub sits next to the deltoid where it bunches under the acromion.
- Across the body: J2 moves over the top and back, and the carriage runs to one end of the track. The anterior track end is closest to the chest.
- Behind the back: J2 moves front-lateral, and the carriage runs to the other end. The posterior track end faces the back.
why_better:
Skin-frame metal: scapula-fixed metal sits on the acromion, and arm-fixed metal (track, bracket, BOTTOM) sits over the arm's quiet lateral strips. Only L1, J2 and a short yoke move in a non-skin frame. The baseline has two 77-81 deg straps plus a floating hub.
Axial range: the axial DOF no longer has to be built from three oblique hubs, so the shoulder pair can be a clean gimbal with its singular poles parked outside the scapula-relative workspace. Kinematic precheck over the 1432 functional poses: a1 = sdir(30,-10) keeps every pose >= 25 deg from both poles (fit clips 29 deg). sdir(40,0) keeps 14 deg (clips 17), sdir(50,10) keeps 10 deg (clips 12).
This tests the user's '2 at the shoulder + rotation farther down' idea head-on.
main_risk:
1. Axial travel. Kinematic precheck (orthogonal gimbal, carriage angle about the humeral axis): the 6 fit clips need only 93/116/138 deg of track for a1 = (30,-10)/(40,0)/(50,10). The functional workspace needs 311/335/353 deg, because its 90-165 deg of axial width at each direction adds to the gimbal's twist across directions. A medially open track cannot exceed ~200 deg, so expect high follow but reach capped around 50-65 %.
2. The singularity-free pole sdir(30,-10) has no hub site: its +pole is inside the abducted arm and its -pole inside the trunk. J1 must therefore tilt to the acromion, trading margin.
3. The yoke rides in the pointing frame over the deltoid while the arm rotates under it.
4. BOTTOM occupies the lateral line (theta ~0, r 56-75 mm) from s ~52 down. A track at s 100 needs BOTTOM cut shorter (top at s ~115) and merged into the track bracket; otherwise the track must sit above BOTTOM's top (s 40-50, deltoid cap, 8-22 mm skin spread).
5. Putting the track 'farther down' (s > 130) turns the yoke into a pointing-frame rib along the arm that must clear BOTTOM's swept tube: out of band.
unpowered_and_mvp2: MVP1: J1 and J2 are O20 hubs on preloaded MR117 pairs. The carriage runs on 4 miniature V-rollers (MR63) on the track's bevelled edges, with a PTFE/needle radial slide and a pin swivel. The arm drives everything through the track; all passive coordinates are geometric, so nothing sags. Use a long carriage so it cannot cock under cuff shear. MVP2: J1 and J2 get cable drums in the hubs (remote motors, Bowden). The axial DOF gets a closed cable loop in the track groove clamped to the carriage (a curved linear drive). Sensing: magnetic encoders in J1/J2, and a magnetic strip along the track read by a Hall sensor on the carriage.
model_spec:
COMMON (bench frame): GH = origin. f = B.frames(i): Rs = f['S'][0] (scapula), Rh = f['H'][0]. A rest-mesh arm point p maps to Rh@p; a scapula-fixed point q maps to Rs@q; M = Rs.T@Rh maps arm vectors into the scapula frame.
Arm axes: e = unit(L['elbow']) = (-0.023,-0.986,0.164) (GH->elbow, 325 mm), l = (0.004,0.164,0.986) lateral, b = (-1,0.023,0) posterior. armpt(s,th,r) = s*e + r*(cos th*l + sin th*b), with th 0 lateral, +90 posterior, -90 anterior.
Scapula directions: sdir(lat,lon) = (-cos lat*sin lon, sin lat, cos lat*cos lon), with lon 0 lateral, +90 posterior, -90 anterior, 180 medial.
circ_int and tri_ok: numpy copies of pipeline/conformal/gpu/band_impl.py.
R_env(s,th): max over all poses of the arm-skin radius about e within (s+-5, th+-3); use the ARMV vertices of B.skin(i) mapped by Rh.T.
RAY FIT (sample with direction u in its member frame): per pose, scan rho downward from 260 mm in 4 mm steps (one B.dist call for all samples) to the first rho with dist < 2 mm, then refine with 3 bisections -> rho_need. Member height = max of rho_need over taken poses, after trimming the 10 % of poses that need the most lift (trimmed poses count as not taken).
Straps: 14 mm wide, skin face sampled every 2 mm. O20 hub: disc r 10; the lower member's skin face sits at the fitted radius, the upper member's underside 3.15 mm higher.
Run two passes: fit, then record. Report inband per group (scapula-fixed / moving / arm-fixed) so quiet-zone ballast cannot inflate the metal-centric score.

GEOMETRY:
- a1 = sdir(40,0). J1 hub on a1 at the fitted radius (~48-55). Its lower member is a 3 mm base plate running posteriorly toward the handler.
- Per pose: d = M@e. Not taken if min(angle(d,a1), angle(d,-a1)) < 10 deg.
- u2 = circ_int(a1, 90deg, d, 90deg, branch=-1) (posterior at rest). J2 = O20 hub on u2 (radius by RAY FIT). L1 = strap along the great circle a1->u2.
- Pointing frame: r_ref = unit(u2-(u2.d)d), t_ref = d x r_ref. Axial angle: lm = M@l, q3 = atan2(lm.t_ref, lm.r_ref).
- The carriage is fixed in the pointing frame at angle th_c0 about d. Its arm-frame angle is th_arm = wrap(th_c0 - q3). Choose th_c0 so the median th_arm over the clip frames equals the track centre (-15 deg).

TRACK (arm-fixed, fitted once):
- Centreline T(th) = s_t*e + (R_env(s_t,th)+4+1.5)*(cos th*l + sin th*b), for th in [-110,80], s_t = 100.
- Section: 8 mm along the arm x 3 mm; sample 3 rows on the skin face at R_env+4.
- Not taken if th_arm is outside [-103,73].
- Carriage: block 24 (along the track) x 16 x 7 mm sitting on T(th_arm).
- Yoke end: fixed in the pointing frame at station s_t, angle th_c0, radius r_y = max over the span of (R_env+4+3) + 7. Sample the radial-slide column (10x10 mm) between the carriage and the yoke end.
- L2 yoke: strap from the J2 hub to the yoke end. Its samples are fixed in [r_ref, t_ref, d]; heights by RAY FIT.
- Bracket: arm-fixed strap from T(0) down the lateral strip, replacing BOTTOM above s 115 (report part interference with the remaining BOTTOM: a 30x6.5 bar from arm_fit.json C_b along u_b).

NOT TAKEN: singular, carriage off the span, contact (bench).
GH translation is not in the bench (GH is fixed in the scapula frame). The radial slide and the optional along-arm float absorb it in reality.
sweep_params: a1 lat 30-55, lon -15..+20 (singular margin vs a housable hub site); alpha12 70-110 and alpha23 70-100 (move J2 off the humeral 'equator'); branch +-1; track station s_t 45-130, plus one point at 250 for the user's 'farther down' extreme; track span centre -40..+20 and width 160-240 deg; th_c0; track gap 3-6 mm.
prior_art: ARMin III: 2-axis shoulder plus a semicircular guide for humeral rotation (Nef, Guidali, Riener 2009). MGA and CADEN-7 use open-ring humeral-rotation bearings. All of these rings are circular and ride in the pointing frame. I know of no arm-fixed, skin-shaped track with a radial+swivel carriage.

name: Scapular race: J1 is a rail on the bony rim and J2 rides its carriage (the only way two GH-concurrent joints can overlap)
topology: Scapula base carrying a fixed arc RAIL. J1 is an active R about a1 through GH; the rail is a circle of angular radius gamma around a1, laid on intrusion-free acromion / scapular-spine / clavicle-rim skin -> rolling carriage. The carriage is L1: there is no link -> J2: O20 hub mounted on the carriage, active R. Its axis is the carriage's own direction from GH, so alpha12 = gamma -> L2 strap, the only moving-frame link -> J3, active R. Default J3: the posterolateral septum barrel on its own arm cuff (see septum-barrel-arm-link). Option: a lateral O20 hub at s 5-30 plus a neck to BOTTOM.
dof_reasoning: Three revolutes with axes concurrent at GH. The rail is a revolute whose bearing is spread along a circle instead of sitting on its own axis, so it counts as one active joint (cable-drivable along the rail, sensable with a magnetic strip). The rollers only realise J1, so there is no passive coordinate and nothing can sag. For real GH/handler translation, add the user-approved passive slides at J3's cuff, outside the count.
description:
Two revolutes with axes through GH can never share a location: their hubs sit on their own axes, and two lines through GH meet only at GH. The rail breaks this, because a revolute's bearing can lie anywhere on a circle around its axis. So J1 becomes a 10 mm wide, 4 mm tall rail fixed to the base, lying ~4 mm over bony, intrusion-free rim. J2 sits on the rail carriage and always rides that quiet rim. The single crossing strap L2 runs from the carriage over the deltoid to J3.
- Rest (precheck geometry): carriage on the posterior/top part of the rim, L2 down the posterior deltoid to the septum barrel.
- Overhead and across the body: the carriage slides along the rim; the rail never moves.
- Behind the back: the carriage goes to the anterior end.
- Poses that would need J2 off the rail are not reachable.
Kinematic hint (also useful for the hub-only GPU family): in the scapula frame, the direction lat 30-40, lon -10..0 is the centre of the arm's workspace. Every arm-fixed hub stays 18-111 deg from it, so a 3R about it needs only 55-60 deg links (total ~115 deg vs the baseline's 77+81). Its pole lies inside the abducted arm, though, so only a race can use it without losing the max-abduction poses. (band_impl allows it: sdir(40,0) has no anterior component.)
why_better: It deletes L1 entirely: the baseline's first 77-deg strap and its floating J2 stack are both gone, leaving one strap as the only moving metal. Intermediate frames have no quiet skin at all. I checked the half-angle frame slerp(S,H,0.5) over the shoulder cap: median skin spread 43 mm, vs 26 in the scapula frame and 30 in the arm frame. Deleting a moving link is therefore the most direct lever on in-band. The rail sits at constant radius over bone, so it is in band by construction.
main_risk:
Reach. Kinematic precheck: I required the used part of the rail to lie on trunk skin that the arm never enters (13-pose probe) with <= 20 mm skin-radius variation. That leaves at best ~45-50 % of the functional workspace. Two best configurations:
- a1 = sdir(0,20), gamma 50, alpha23 80, branch +1, J3 septum barrel: J2 phi -104..+64, skin R 45-61 mm.
- a1 = sdir(40,-100), gamma 70, alpha23 70, branch -1: phi 20..116.
Without the skin constraint the chain closes in 92-99 % of poses (a1 = sdir(40,0), gamma = alpha23 = 60), but J2 must circle ~280 deg, through the arm.
So this is probably a high-band, low-reach clip/overhead specialist. A constant-radius rail over 44-62 mm skin also varies its gap by up to 18 mm. (My intrusion filter is conservative: one probe pose was enough to veto a bin.)
unpowered_and_mvp2: MVP1: carriage on 4-6 preloaded V-rollers (MR63/MR74) on a Ti rail with ground 90-deg edges; J2 and J3 are O20 hubs. No spare, nothing sags, rolling friction only. MVP2: J1 is driven by a cable loop in the rail groove clamped to the carriage (remote motor); J2 and J3 by hub drums. Sensing: magnetic strip + Hall on the carriage for J1, magnetic encoders for J2/J3.
model_spec:
COMMON (bench frame): GH = origin. f = B.frames(i): Rs = f['S'][0], Rh = f['H'][0]. A rest-mesh arm point p maps to Rh@p; a scapula-fixed point q maps to Rs@q; M = Rs.T@Rh.
Arm axes: e = unit(L['elbow']) = (-0.023,-0.986,0.164), l = (0.004,0.164,0.986), b = (-1,0.023,0). armpt(s,th,r) = s*e + r*(cos th*l + sin th*b) (th 0 lateral, +90 posterior).
Scapula directions: sdir(lat,lon) = (-cos lat*sin lon, sin lat, cos lat*cos lon) (lon 0 lateral, +90 posterior, -90 anterior).
circ_int and tri_ok: numpy copies of band_impl.py.
R_env(s,th): max over poses of the arm-skin radius about e (ARMV vertices of B.skin(i) mapped by Rh.T).
RAY FIT: per pose, scan rho downward from 260 mm in 4 mm steps to the first rho with B.dist < 2 mm, then 3 bisections -> rho_need. Height = max over taken poses after trimming the worst 10 % of poses (those count as not taken).
Straps: 14 mm wide, skin face sampled every 2 mm. O20 hub: disc r 10; upper member +3.15 mm. Two passes. Report inband per group.

GEOMETRY:
- a1 = sdir(0,20). m = unit(y - (y.a1)a1) (phi = 0 up), n = a1 x m (phi = +90 posterior).
- Rail = {cos g*a1 + sin g*(cos phi*m + sin phi*n)}, g = 50 deg, phi in [phi_lo,phi_hi] = [-115,75] (trim to the used phi range after pass 1).
- J3 axis: w = unit(armpt(150,35,R_env(150,35)+9)) (septum barrel; the precheck used th = 20, 35 clears BOTTOM). Option: w = unit(armpt(30,0,80)) with an O20 hub plus a neck strap down the lateral strip to armpt(65,0,R_env+4). alpha23 = 80.
- Per pose: u3 = M@w. Require tri_ok(a1,u3,g,a23,8deg). u2 = circ_int(a1,g,u3,a23,+1). phi = atan2(u2.n, u2.m). Not taken if phi is outside [phi_lo+8, phi_hi-8] (carriage +-8 deg).

METAL:
- Rail: scapula-fixed band 10 mm wide along the arc, sampled every 3 deg x 3 rows. Skin face at rho_r - 4, where rho_r = 6 + RAY FIT max over taken poses of the arc samples.
- Carriage: 26 x 22 x 8 mm centred at u2*rho_r, sharing the rail's skin face.
- J2: O20 hub on the carriage; L2's underside near J2 at rho_r+4.15.
- L2: strap along the great circle u2->u3, sampled in L2's frame [u2, unit(u3-(u3.u2)u2), cross], heights by RAY FIT.
- J3: barrel as in septum-barrel-arm-link (cylinder r 7, length 24 along w, proximal end 2 mm over the skin) or the O20 hub + neck.

NOT TAKEN: tri_ok/closure fail, phi off the rail, contact.
sweep_params: Race axis a1: lat -10..50, lon -110..+40. gamma 40-80. alpha23 50-100. Rail arc limits phi_lo/phi_hi. Branch. J3 choice (septum barrel s 120-200 / th 25-40, or lateral hub s 5-30 + neck). Trim fraction 0-20 %.
prior_art: Same curved-guide principle as ARMin III's humeral-rotation guide (Nef et al. 2009), and as telescope alt-az races and turntable bearings. I know of no shoulder exo that puts the first joint on a scapula-fixed race carrying the second hub.

name: Septum barrel: near-axial J3 lying along the quietest arm strip on its own cuff (the humerus is the link to BOTTOM)
topology: Scapula base -> J1: O20 hub, active R, a1 = sdir(55,15) on the acromion top -> L1 strap -> J2: O20 hub, active R, floating -> L2 strap -> J3: BARREL hinge, active R. Its axis passes through GH and is aimed down the posterolateral septum strip, 17-24 deg off the humeral axis, so the barrel lies ALONG the arm with its axis nearly tangent to the skin -> a separate proximal arm cuff (saddle) at s 120-180, th 30-40, beside BOTTOM. No neck: the humerus itself is the rigid link between this cuff and the user's cuff/BOTTOM.
dof_reasoning: Spherical 3R with all axes through GH: exactly 3 active revolutes and no passive coordinate. The proximal cuff is a second skin attachment, not a joint. For real GH/handler translation, the user-approved passive slides (along-arm + tangential) go between the barrel cuff and the arm, outside the count.
description:
Joints sit where the rig's skin moves least.
- J1 sits on the bony acromion top (2-5 mm skin spread in the scapula frame).
- J3 sits on the posterolateral intermuscular-septum strip. In the arm frame, th 0..45 deg and s 120-240 mm from GH, the material-point radial spread over 13 poses is only 0.7-1.6 mm, the quietest skin on the body model (the anterolateral strip, -45..0, is 2-4 mm).
- An axis through GH can only be tangent to skin along the arm, so J3 there is a barrel: two MR117 back-to-back, OD 14, 24 mm long, lying along the arm, rather than a hub standing 12.25 mm off it.
Metal by pose:
- Rest: barrel on the posterolateral arm ~150 mm below GH beside BOTTOM; L2 climbs the posterior deltoid to J2 behind the shoulder; L1 crosses to the acromion.
- Overhead: the barrel faces back/up with the raised arm; J2 sits over the posterior-superior scapula; L1 short over the top.
- Across the body: the barrel faces back/out; L2 wraps over the posterior deltoid.
- Behind the back: the barrel faces out/up; J2 sits lateral of the acromion.
why_better:
1. The arm-end neck disappears. On the r20 picks, every evaluator part collision was 'link 2 - neck', and the hub-arm-end neck caused most of R16's part interference.
2. Arm-fixed metal sits only on the quietest strip.
3. The barrel's skin face is 2-12 mm along its length, instead of a 12.25 mm hub stack plus a neck.
It is a direct test of whether J3 belongs in the quiet strip. Today the GPU picks put it high on the deltoid at 69-71 deg off the arm axis, where arm-frame skin spread is 8-22 mm.
main_risk:
1. J3 is now nearly the humeral axis, so q3 carries most of the axial rotation (+-75 deg at a given direction). L2 and J2 swing around the deltoid cap relative to the arm skin, and the cap is 50-82 mm from the humeral axis depending on azimuth.
2. L1 gets long. Kinematic band from the acromion to the septum point (s150, th 20) is 55-150 deg (p5-p95), so alpha12 ~100 and alpha23 ~50. With the central axis sdir(35,-5) the band is 29-128 deg (-> 75/55).
3. A GH-aimed line converges on the humeral axis proximally, so the barrel must be short: its underside rises ~10 mm over 24 mm.
4. A second cuff adds skin pressure (R11), and the barrel cuff must clear BOTTOM (30 mm wide at th ~0, r 56-75 mm).
unpowered_and_mvp2: MVP1: J1 and J2 are O20 hubs. J3 is two MR117 in the barrel sleeve on an integral Ti pin of the cuff. No spare joint, rolling friction. MVP2: J3 gets a cable drum turned on the barrel sleeve, with the Bowden running down the arm next to BOTTOM (easy routing). J1 and J2 get hub drums. Magnetic encoder at the barrel's distal end.

COMMON (bench frame): GH = origin. f = B.frames(i): Rs = f['S'][0], Rh = f['H'][0]. Arm point p maps to Rh@p; scapula point q maps to Rs@q; M = Rs.T@Rh.
Arm axes: e = unit(L['elbow']) = (-0.023,-0.986,0.164), l = (0.004,0.164,0.986), b = (-1,0.023,0). armpt(s,th,r) = s*e + r*(cos th*l + sin th*b).
Scapula directions: sdir(lat,lon) = (-cos lat*sin lon, sin lat, cos lat*cos lon).
circ_int and tri_ok from band_impl.py.
R_env(s,th): max over poses of the arm-skin radius about e (ARMV vertices of B.skin(i) mapped by Rh.T).
RAY FIT: per pose, scan rho downward from 260 mm in 4 mm steps to the first rho with B.dist < 2, refine -> rho_need. Height = max over taken poses after a 10 % trim. Straps 14 mm wide, sampled every 2 mm; O20 hub = disc r 10, upper member +3.15. Two passes. Report inband per group.

J3 / BARREL:
- Station s_b = 150, th_b = 35. Barrel centre c = armpt(s_b, th_b, R_env(s_b,th_b)+9+k). Raise k until the proximal end (c - 12*w) clears the skin by 2 mm.
- w = unit(c) is J3's arm-fixed axis.
- Barrel: cylinder r 7, length 24 along w; sample its skin-facing half-surface as 3 lines.
- Cuff saddle: arm-fixed, 40 (around) x 50 (along) x 3 mm under the barrel at R_env+2 (liner). Report it as group 'cuff'.
- Check the barrel/cuff against BOTTOM: a 30 x 6.5 bar from pipeline/full-exo/arm_fit.json C_b along u_b, 265 mm. Require > 2 mm clearance.

CHAIN:
- a1 = sdir(55,15), alpha12 = 100, alpha23 = 50 (alternative: a1 = sdir(35,-5) with 75/55).
- Per pose: u3 = M@w. Not taken unless tri_ok(a1,u3,a12,a23,8deg). u2 = circ_int(a1,a12,u3,a23,branch).
- O20 hubs at a1 and u2 (RAY FIT radius).
- L1: strap a1->u2.
- L2: strap from u2 to the barrel's proximal end, attached to the sleeve. Its samples are fixed in L2's frame [u3, unit(u2-(u2.u3)u3), cross], which rotates with J2 and J3.
- RAY FIT for L1, L2 and the J2 hub.

NOT TAKEN: closure/tri_ok fail, contact, barrel vs BOTTOM.
sweep_params: Barrel station s_b 110-210. th_b 25-45 (beside BOTTOM) or -40..-20 (anterolateral strip). Barrel length 18-30. J1 site: acromion sdir(55,15), central sdir(35,-5) or posterior-superior sdir(40,95). alpha12 60-110, alpha23 40-70. Branch.
prior_art: Exos usually do humeral rotation with a ring or arc around the upper arm (ARMin III, CADEN-7, MGA). I know of no design that uses a GH-aimed barrel lying along the arm as the last joint of a spherical chain, nor one that removes the arm-end neck by treating the humerus as the link between two cuffs.

name: Scapular skate: J1 is a puck gliding on a flat plate on the back of the shoulder (remote-centre rotation, passive in-plane slip)
topology: Scapula base = a flat Ti plate (3 mm, ~110 x 90 mm), parallel to the posterior scapular skin plane (fitted normal ~sdir(27,75), ~59 mm behind GH) -> SKATE: a puck on a ball cage under a retaining lip. It has 3 planar coordinates: the in-plane rotation is the active J1 (about the plate normal through GH, a remote axis with no hub), and the 2 in-plane translations are passive -> J2: O20 hub on the puck, active R. Its axis runs from GH through the puck point and is tilted ~55 deg to the plate -> L2 strap -> J3: active R, either an O20 hub at armpt(30,40,~80) plus a neck to BOTTOM, or the septum barrel.
dof_reasoning: The puck has 3 planar DOF on the plate. J2's axis must pass through GH, because L2, J3 and the arm are all concurrent at GH. That imposes 2 conditions on the puck, so its two translations are set by closure and only the in-plane rotation remains: J1 = rotation about the plate normal through GH, active (driven and sensed). The passive slides have no free direction once the chain closes, so nothing sags. In the real world they move only with the handler slip / GH translation in the scapular plane, which they absorb. A concurrent chain cannot do that: R10 is design-independent for spherical chains, and is 15 mm today vs 4 allowed.
description:
A rotation about the normal of a flat region maps that plane onto itself. So everything J1 carries on the plate (puck, J2's base) stays at constant height over the flat back of the shoulder, whatever q1 is. There is no L1 swinging through the air and no J1 hub on the shoulder top.
- Rest: the puck sits on the infraspinatus ~84 mm from the foot of GH on the plate, J2 tilted on it, L2 down the posterior deltoid to J3 on the posterolateral upper arm.
- Overhead: the puck rotates along its arc toward the spine/upper plate; L2 shortens over the top-back.
- Across the body: the puck moves toward the medial/upper part of the plate.
- Behind the back: the puck swings toward the lateral/lower edge; this is where it may leave the flat region.
The plate is base metal over the scapula's quiet skin (0.2-2.4 mm Lagrangian spread at lat 30-60, lon 60-120).
why_better:
1. The links are flat by geometry: the J1 'link' cannot leave the skin plane.
2. The 12.25 mm J1 stack disappears.
3. A built-in R10 absorber: none of the concurrent chains can fix the 15 mm handler-slip misalignment without a passive element, and here the passive element is the joint itself.
4. Total moving metal is one strap (L2) plus the J2 hub.
main_risk:
1. The posterior skin is less flat and less scapula-fixed than hoped. A plane fit over 219 x 165 mm has 9.6 mm rms (31 mm max), and those trunk points drift 12 mm (median; 29 mm p90) from the plane across the 13 probe poses. So keep the plate to ~110 x 90 mm near lat 0-45, lon 60-120.
2. The kinematic band from the plate normal to the s30 posterolateral hub is 35-145 deg, so alpha12 ~55 (J2 84 mm from the foot point) and alpha23 ~90. The puck sweeps an 84 mm-radius arc and leaves the plate for large q1.
3. J2's hub stands 55 deg tilted on the puck, so one rim is ~8 mm higher.
4. MVP2 has to drive a remote-centre rotation by cable, which is awkward.
unpowered_and_mvp2: MVP1: puck on a ball cage (or PTFE pads) captured under the plate lip, with low friction. The arm drives the puck through L2 and closure fixes its path. Gravity on the puck's slip is carried by the closure; check friction in the slip direction under cuff load (R17). MVP2: two antagonistic Bowden cables pull the puck along its arc (anchored at the plate edges, acting through a pulley-free cable saddle on the puck). Puck pose (x, y, theta) is sensed by two planar optical/magnetic sensors, with theta as the joint value. The slip stays passive and unpowered.
