COMMON (bench frame): GH = origin. f = B.frames(i): Rs = f['S'][0], Rh = f['H'][0]. Arm point p maps to Rh@p; scapula point q maps to Rs@q; M = Rs.T@Rh.
Arm axes: e = unit(L['elbow']) = (-0.023,-0.986,0.164), l = (0.004,0.164,0.986), b = (-1,0.023,0). armpt(s,th,r) = s*e + r*(cos th*l + sin th*b).
Scapula directions: sdir(lat,lon) = (-cos lat*sin lon, sin lat, cos lat*cos lon).
circ_int and tri_ok from band_impl.py. R_env(s,th) from the ARMV skin in the arm frame.
RAY FIT: scan rho downward from 260 mm in 4 mm steps to the first rho with B.dist < 2, refine -> rho_need. Height = max over taken poses after a 10 % trim. Straps 14 mm wide, sampled every 2 mm; O20 hub = disc r 10, +3.15. Two passes. Report inband per group.

PLATE:
- Map the non-ARMV skin vertices of a rest-pose B.skin(i) into the scapula frame with Rs.T. Keep lat 0-45, lon 60-120. Fit a plane by SVD: normal n_p (posterior), offset h (expect ~59 mm), foot point F = h*n_p.
- a1 = n_p.
- Plate: 110 x 90 mm outline centred on the fitted patch, 3 mm thick, parallel to the plane at offset h_p = 2 + max over all poses of (the skin's height above the plane within the outline). Sample its skin face (scapula-fixed).

CHAIN:
- alpha12 = 55, alpha23 = 90, w = unit(armpt(30,40,80)).
- Per pose: u3 = M@w. Not taken unless tri_ok(a1,u3,55,90,8deg).
- u2 = circ_int(a1,55deg,u3,90deg,branch). Puck point P = (h_p+3)/(u2.n_p)*u2 (where J2's axis pierces the puck top). Not taken if P is closer than 25 mm to the plate outline.

METAL:
- Puck: disc r 25, 6 mm tall; underside = plate top + 0.5.
- J2: O20 hub with axis u2 on the puck. Sample its disc underside, which is tilted.
- L2: strap from the J2 hub to J3, in L2's frame, RAY FIT.
- J3: O20 hub on u3 (RAY FIT) + neck: arm-fixed strap down the posterolateral/lateral strip to armpt(65,0,R_env+4) (BOTTOM's top).

NOT TAKEN: closure, puck off the plate, contact.
The bench has no GH translation; to show the slip benefit, separately perturb GH by 10-15 mm in-plane and confirm the puck stays on the plate.
sweep_params: Plate patch centre (lat 0-40, lon 60-120) and size (80-130 mm). alpha12 40-60 (puck arc radius h*tan(alpha12)). alpha23 70-110. J3 site (s 5-40, th 0-45) or septum barrel. Branch. Plate offset margin.
prior_art: Passive scapular translation stages in shoulder exos are used to follow the girdle (e.g. Harmony's shoulder girdle mechanism; self-aligning designs after Schiele & van der Helm 2006, Stienen et al. 2009 Dampace). Using a planar skate as a remote-centre first joint, with its slip as the closure, is not known to me.

name: Skin-normal hubs + passive cuff translation stage (non-concurrent 3R placed on the flattest quiet seats)
topology: Scapula base -> J1: O20 hub, active R. Its axis is the skin NORMAL at the acromion seat, not through GH; the line passes ~5-20 mm from GH -> L1 -> J2: O20 hub, active R. Its axis is the skin normal at its home seat on the posterior-superior zone -> L2 -> J3: active R, either a septum barrel or a lateral hub with axis through GH -> passive XYZ translation stage (along the arm on a short rail merged into BOTTOM's top, tangential, radial; +-25 mm) -> arm cuff/BOTTOM.
dof_reasoning: Orientation is carried by the three active revolutes; only their directions matter for orientation. Their lines do not meet at GH, so the chain end is displaced from the arm attachment by a pose-dependent translation, and the 3 passive slides take exactly that displacement. Chain + stage has 6 DOF for the arm's 6 equations (3 rotations about the human GH plus its translation): determinate, no spare, closed through the arm's own joint. The same stage absorbs the handler slip and GH translation (R10).
description:
Each hub stands square on its seat: the 12.25 mm stack is normal to the skin. Seats are chosen purely by quietness and flatness: J1 on the bony acromion, J2's home on the posterior-superior zone (0.2-2.4 mm spread). A GH-radial hub on sloping skin sits tilted, and an O20 rim then rises 10*sin(tilt), i.e. 5-8 mm on the 20-30 deg slopes of the posterior shoulder; the stack being normal removes that.
- Rest: J1 flat on the acromion, J2 flat on the supraspinous area, L2 down the posterior deltoid to J3, stage at BOTTOM's top.
- Overhead / across the body / behind the back: as for a 3R with these axis directions, plus the stage sliding by the offset-induced error (expected 10-60 mm).
why_better:
1. A small direct in-band gain from flat hub seats.
2. The structural point: it is the one concurrent-axis escape that keeps 3 active joints and gets R10 (handler slip, 15 mm today, independent of design for any GH-concurrent chain) under control by design, with the user-approved passive cuff slides as part of the kinematics rather than an afterthought.
3. Seat choice is freed from the GH-radial constraint.
main_risk:
1. Stage travel and metal: the stage moves ~sum of 2*d_k*sin(q_k/2). Axis offsets of 10-20 mm over 100-150 deg swings give 30-60 mm, and a 3-axis stage on the arm is heavy and tall.
2. The radial slide changes the arm-end height.
3. The bench has GH fixed to the scapula, so it shows only the cost, not the R10 benefit.
4. The skin normals over the shoulder cap pass near GH anyway, so the in-band gain may be small.
Honest expectation: a modest bench score, valuable mainly for R10.
unpowered_and_mvp2: MVP1: O20 hubs. Stage = three crossed miniature ball slides (7 mm rails) or the user's passive cuff slides. Free, and positioned by the arm through closure; check that gravity on the stage's vertical axis does not load the arm (R17: <= 5 N at the cuff). MVP2: the three hubs get cable drums; the stage is never powered or sensed.
model_spec:
COMMON (bench frame): GH = origin. f = B.frames(i): Rs = f['S'][0], Rh = f['H'][0]. Arm point p maps to Rh@p; scapula point q maps to Rs@q; M = Rs.T@Rh.
Arm axes: e = unit(L['elbow']) = (-0.023,-0.986,0.164), l = (0.004,0.164,0.986), b = (-1,0.023,0). armpt(s,th,r) = s*e + r*(cos th*l + sin th*b).
Scapula directions: sdir(lat,lon) = (-cos lat*sin lon, sin lat, cos lat*cos lon).
R_env from the ARMV skin. RAY FIT: scan rho downward from 260 mm in 4 mm steps to the first rho with B.dist < 2 -> rho_need; 10 % trim. O20 hub = disc r 10, +3.15. Straps 14 mm wide, sampled every 2 mm. Two passes. Report inband per group.

SEATS (rest pose, scapula frame):
- J1: P1 = skin point along sdir(55,15) + 2 mm; n1 = mean outward face normal within 10 mm of it.
- J2 home: P2 = skin along sdir(40,95) + 2; n2 likewise.
- J3: axis line through GH with direction w = unit(armpt(30,40,80)) (hub at its RAY FIT radius), or the septum barrel.

ORIENTATION IK:
- Directions (n1, n2, w) with q = 0 at the rest pose.
- Solve R(n1,q1) R(R(n1,q1)n2... i.e. the standard product R(n1,q1)*R(n2,q2)*R(w,q3) = M*M0^-1 (M0 = the rest pose's M) with Paden-Kahan subproblems 2 then 1, or scipy least_squares warm-started from the previous pose. Keep the branch continuous from home.
- Not taken if the Jacobian condition is > 50 (singular).

POSITION FK:
- J2 line = rotate (P2, n2) about line (P1, n1) by q1.
- J3 attachment point A_chain = the member point rotated about the J2 line by q2, and so on.
- Arm attachment A_arm = M@armpt(65,0,R_env+4).
- Delta = A_chain - A_arm in the arm frame [e, tangential, radial]. Not taken if any |component| > 25 mm (stage travel).

METAL: hubs as O20 discs on their lines at their seats (moving with their members); straps between hub centres (RAY FIT in member frames); stage block 30 x 30 x 10 mm (arm-fixed) at A_arm. Also report the stage displacement distribution.
sweep_params: Seat locations for J1 (acromion top, lateral acromion) and J2 (posterior-superior lat 30-55, lon 70-120). Blend between skin normal and GH-radial direction (0..1; 0 = the spherical chain). Stage travel limit 15-35 mm. J3 choice.
prior_art: Self-aligning exoskeleton axes through decoupling of rotations and translations: Dampace (Stienen et al. 2009); kinematic compatibility (Schiele & van der Helm 2006); kinetostatic self-alignment (Cempini et al. 2013); ABLE and Harmony shoulder girdle mechanisms. None placed the hubs by skin flatness/quietness.

name: Front route: J1 on the bony acromio-clavicular front, crossing the anterior shoulder to the anterolateral strip (short links; the GPU never looked here)
topology: Scapula base + a scapula-fixed bridge strap from the handler over the acromion top to the front seat -> J1: O20 hub, active R, a1 = sdir(40,-100) over the AC joint / lateral clavicle -> L1 (alpha12 ~60) -> J2: O20 hub, active R, floating in front of / over the top of the shoulder -> L2 (alpha23 ~60) -> J3: active R, an O20 hub on the anterolateral upper arm at armpt(30,-40,~76) plus a neck down the anterolateral strip (th -45..0) to BOTTOM's top. Option: an anterolateral septum barrel at s 150, th -30.
dof_reasoning: A spherical 3R: three active revolutes, all through GH, no passive coordinate. The bridge is part of the scapula-fixed base. Handle GH/handler translation with the usual passive cuff slides, outside the count.
description:
Most of the functional workspace is forward (planes 30-150). This route puts the scapula anchor near the centre of that forward motion, on bone (acromion front / clavicle), and lands J3 on the anterolateral arm strip (2-4 mm spread).
- Rest: J1 in front of the acromion, J2 over the anterolateral deltoid, J3 high on the anterolateral arm, neck down the strip, bridge over the acromion.
- Overhead (scaption/flexion): the chain folds over the front-top of the shoulder with the two links overlapping. It folds rather than stretches, with an 8 deg fold margin.
- Across the body: J1 is closest to the arm/hand.
- Behind the back: the chain stretches over the front-lateral shoulder.
why_better: Kinematic band from AC-front sdir(40,-100) to the s30 anterolateral point is 21-115 deg over the workspace (21-110 on the clips). So alpha12 = alpha23 = 60 covers ~95 % of poses at 8 deg singular margins, with total link arc 120 deg vs the baseline's 158 (~25 % less moving metal). The clavicle-lateral seat sdir(30,-80) gives 17-102 (-> 55/55). This region is unexplored: band_impl rejects any J1 with an anterior component > 0.15 (b_ant_max) because there was no back anchor, and the scapula-fixed bridge over the acromion provides one.
main_risk:
1. The front seat is not as quiet as the back: scapula-frame skin at lat 30-45, lon -90..-120 has 8-11 mm spread, and the arm/hand reaches it in 8-38 % of the probe poses (across the body, comb hair). Across-body reach may collapse.
2. J2 floats over the anterior deltoid / biceps root (arm-frame spread 10-15 mm).
3. The bridge adds ~80-100 mm of base strap (in band, but mass).
4. The front of the shoulder is where the shoulder-pad cover and clothing straps go.
unpowered_and_mvp2: MVP1: three O20 hubs, rolling, no spare. MVP2: hub drums, with Bowdens routed from the back over the bridge.
model_spec:
COMMON (bench frame): GH = origin. f = B.frames(i): Rs = f['S'][0], Rh = f['H'][0]. Arm point p maps to Rh@p; scapula point q maps to Rs@q; M = Rs.T@Rh.
Arm axes: e = unit(L['elbow']) = (-0.023,-0.986,0.164), l = (0.004,0.164,0.986), b = (-1,0.023,0). armpt(s,th,r) = s*e + r*(cos th*l + sin th*b).
Scapula directions: sdir(lat,lon) = (-cos lat*sin lon, sin lat, cos lat*cos lon).
circ_int and tri_ok from band_impl.py. R_env from the ARMV skin.
RAY FIT: scan rho downward from 260 mm in 4 mm steps to the first rho with B.dist < 2 -> rho_need; 10 % trim. Straps 14 mm wide, sampled every 2 mm; O20 hub = disc r 10, +3.15. Two passes. Report inband per group.

CHAIN:
- a1 = sdir(40,-100), w = unit(armpt(30,-40,76)), alpha12 = alpha23 = 60.
- Per pose: u3 = M@w. Not taken unless tri_ok(a1,u3,60deg,60deg,8deg).
- u2 = circ_int(a1,60deg,u3,60deg,branch); pick the branch that puts J2 outside the arm at rest.

METAL:
- O20 hubs on a1, u2, u3, each at its RAY FIT radius.
- L1 and L2: straps on the great circles a1->u2 and u2->u3, sampled in their link frames, RAY FIT.
- Base bridge (scapula-fixed): strap 14 x 3 from sdir(45,90) (handler side) via sdir(65,20) to the J1 seat; heights = RAY FIT max over poses.
- Neck (arm-fixed): strap from the J3 hub down armpt(s,-30,R_env+4) to s = 65, then laterally to armpt(65,0,R_env+4) (BOTTOM's top).

NOT TAKEN: closure/tri_ok fail, contact.
sweep_params: J1 seat: AC-front sdir(35-45,-90..-110), clavicle-lateral sdir(25-35,-70..-90), supraclavicular sdir(45-55,-130..-150) (needs alpha ~95/55). alpha12/alpha23 50-100. J3: s 5-40, th -60..-10, or an anterolateral barrel. Branch.
prior_art: Shoulder exos with the first actuator in front of or above the shoulder (e.g. ARMin's front-mounted axes on a fixed frame; the Harmony shoulder). On a scapula-riding base with a back anchor, this route was excluded from our own search by b_ant_max = 0.15.

name: Scapular five-bar + twist: both pointing joints are scapula-fixed hubs on the two quietest seats (bold)
topology: Scapula base with TWO fixed active hubs: A on the acromion top, sdir(55,15); B on the posterior-superior zone, sdir(40,100) -> proximal straps L_A (alpha_A) and L_B (alpha_B) -> passive elbow hubs E_A and E_B -> distal straps D_A (beta_A) and D_B (beta_B) -> these meet at C, an arm-fixed site at armpt(30,0,~80) with a stacked double O20 hub. At C, the D_A-D_B joint is passive and the D_B-arm joint is the active twist about GH-C. All axes pass through GH: a spherical 2-DOF five-bar plus a coaxial twist, ending in a neck to BOTTOM.
dof_reasoning: A spherical five-bar (5 links, 5 revolutes) has mobility 2. With both base joints active, it fixes the direction of GH-C on the arm, and the coaxial twist adds the rotation about GH-C: 3 active in total. The two elbows and the coupler pivot are fixed by the five-bar closure for given A and B (each leg's branch is chosen once), so there is no undriven coordinate and nothing sags. Joint count is 6, more than the user would like.
description:
Both pointing actuators and their hubs are scapula-fixed on the quietest seats (acromion top 2-5 mm, posterior-superior 0.2-2.4 mm). The four straps converge on C on the upper lateral arm.
- Rest: leg A runs down the lateral shoulder, leg B over the posterior deltoid, C on the lateral deltoid with the neck to BOTTOM.
- Overhead: both legs fold over the top-back as C rises.
- Across the body: leg B stretches; leg A folds over the top.
- Behind the back: leg A stretches forward-lateral; leg B folds.
why_better:
1. MVP2 routing is simplest of all concepts: the two pointing motors' cables end on the base, and no cable crosses a moving joint except the twist.
2. Two load paths: lower tilt moments per bearing (relevant for MVP2's ~10 N.m, which already exceeds a single MR117 pair's C0 if carried as tilt).
3. Singularities move: a five-bar fails at leg fold/stretch or when the distal arms align at C, not when three serial axes become coplanar. This may free regions of the workspace the serial 3R loses.
main_risk:
1. Twice the moving metal. Kinematic bands: acromion -> C is 25-138 deg (-> alpha_A = beta_A = 72); posterior -> C is 57-162 deg (-> alpha_B ~110, beta_B ~55). That is ~310 deg of straps crossing the shoulder vs 158 in the baseline, so in-band will probably drop.
2. Reach is the intersection of both legs' reach.
3. Four straps converge on the deltoid at C, where the bulge is.
4. Six joints vs the user's wish for 3.
unpowered_and_mvp2: MVP1: six bearing sets (C stacked: two MR117 pairs), rolling. Closure holds all the passive joints; leg weight is shared. MVP2: A and B get hub drums with base-fixed Bowden stops; the twist at C gets a drum on the arm. Magnetic encoders at A, B and C.
model_spec:
COMMON (bench frame): GH = origin. f = B.frames(i): Rs = f['S'][0], Rh = f['H'][0]. Arm point p maps to Rh@p; scapula point q maps to Rs@q; M = Rs.T@Rh.
Arm axes: e = unit(L['elbow']) = (-0.023,-0.986,0.164), l = (0.004,0.164,0.986), b = (-1,0.023,0). armpt(s,th,r) = s*e + r*(cos th*l + sin th*b).
Scapula directions: sdir(lat,lon) = (-cos lat*sin lon, sin lat, cos lat*cos lon).
circ_int and tri_ok from band_impl.py. R_env from the ARMV skin.
RAY FIT: scan rho downward from 260 mm in 4 mm steps to the first rho with B.dist < 2 -> rho_need; 10 % trim. Straps 14 mm wide, sampled every 2 mm; O20 hub = disc r 10, +3.15. Two passes. Report inband per group.

CHAIN:
- uA = sdir(55,15), uB = sdir(40,100), w = unit(armpt(30,0,80)).
- alpha_A = beta_A = 72, alpha_B = 110, beta_B = 55.
- Per pose: uC = M@w.
- E_A = circ_int(uA,alpha_A,uC,beta_A,sA), E_B = circ_int(uB,alpha_B,uC,beta_B,sB). Fix sA and sB at the rest pose so both elbows are outside the arm's path.
- Valid only if both legs pass tri_ok (8 deg), and the transmission angle at C is within [20,160] deg (angle between the tangents at C of the arcs C->E_A and C->E_B; outside it is a five-bar singularity). Otherwise not taken.
- Twist angle (for the report): rotation of M@l about uC relative to D_B's frame.

METAL:
- Base hubs at uA and uB (scapula-fixed), elbow hubs at E_A and E_B, and the C hub stacked twice (2 x 3.15 mm).
- Four straps along their great circles, each sampled in its own link frame: L_A in [uA,E_A], D_A in [E_A,uC], L_B in [uB,E_B], D_B in [E_B,uC]. RAY FIT for each.
- Neck: from C down the lateral strip to armpt(65,0,R_env+4).

NOT TAKEN: leg closure, transmission angle, contact.
sweep_params: Base seats A (acromion / lateral acromion) and B (posterior-superior lat 25-55, lon 70-130). alpha_A, beta_A, alpha_B, beta_B 40-120. Leg branches. C site (s 5-40, th -20..40). Transmission-angle limit.
prior_art: Spherical parallel manipulators: Gosselin's spherical five-bar and the Agile Eye (Gosselin & Hamel 1994). Spherical-parallel shoulder exoskeleton prototypes exist in the rehabilitation literature, typically with ground-mounted bases, not a scapula-riding one.

name: GH tripod: three telescoping struts from quiet scapular seats to quiet arm strips, with the human shoulder as the spherical joint (bold / weird)
topology:
Three legs, each U - P - U:
- U: passive cardan on a scapula-fixed seat.
- P: active telescoping strut, Ti tube in tube, OD 8.
- U: passive cardan on an arm-fixed seat (a small proximal cuff, or BOTTOM's outer face).
The exo has no rotation centre; the human GH is the only spherical constraint (a 3-UPU parallel mechanism about the human joint).
dof_reasoning: The arm has 3 rotational DOF about its own GH. Each strut length is one scalar function of arm orientation, so the 3 lengths determine it wherever the three strut moment vectors about GH are independent. U-P-U legs have no free spin about their own axis (an S joint would add an undriven, floppy spin). All 12 universal-joint angles are set by the leg geometry, so nothing sags. Active = the 3 measured lengths; in MVP2 a Bowden pulling a slider is the most natural cable actuator there is.
description:
Scapula seats sit on the quietest base skin: B1 acromion top, B2 posterior-superior, B3 posterior scapula at GH level. Arm seats sit on the quiet strips: C1 anterolateral at s 110, C2 posterolateral at s 150, C3 on BOTTOM's outer face at s ~220.
- Rest: three struts fan down from the top/back of the shoulder to the lateral arm.
- Overhead: the arm seats rise above the shoulder, and the struts shorten and bunch over the top.
- Across the body: the posterior struts stretch over the back of the arm.
- Behind the back: the anterior strut stretches over the front.
There are no hubs anywhere on the shoulder cap.
why_better:
1. It is the only concept whose kinematics do not depend on matching the GH centre, so handler slip and GH translation (R10: 15 mm today, design-independent for every concurrent chain) vanish by construction.
2. No 12 mm hub stacks over the shoulder, only small cardans on quiet seats.
3. It maps 1:1 onto MVP2 Bowden actuation.
4. It is cheap to model. Even if it fails the 1 cm rule, it bounds how much proximity a non-rotary topology loses.
main_risk:
1. Straight members over a convex, bulging shoulder: a chord between a scapular seat and an arm seat passes through the deltoid unless it stands off. Expect most strut length out of band and many poses with a strut inside the deltoid.
2. Extension ratio: an arm seat moves ~200 mm between rest and overhead, so telescopes need ~2:1.
3. Singular poses where the three moment vectors become coplanar (to be measured).
4. It relies on the arm's own GH: soft-tissue compliance at the cuffs becomes tracking error, and the assist load in MVP2 passes through the human joint.
I expect this to score poorly on in-band. Its value is as a bound and as an R10-free reference.
unpowered_and_mvp2: MVP1: Ti tube-in-tube struts on linear ball bushings or PTFE, light (gravity torque about GH counts against R17); miniature cardans with MR52 bearings. No spare. MVP2: each inner tube pulled by a push-pull Bowden or an antagonistic pair; length sensed by a magnetic linear encoder inside the tube.
model_spec:
COMMON (bench frame): GH = origin. f = B.frames(i): Rs = f['S'][0], Rh = f['H'][0]. Arm point p maps to Rh@p; scapula point q maps to Rs@q.
Arm axes: e = unit(L['elbow']) = (-0.023,-0.986,0.164), l = (0.004,0.164,0.986), b = (-1,0.023,0). armpt(s,th,r) = s*e + r*(cos th*l + sin th*b).
Scapula directions: sdir(lat,lon) = (-cos lat*sin lon, sin lat, cos lat*cos lon).
R_env(s,th): max over poses of the arm-skin radius about e (ARMV vertices mapped by Rh.T). Report inband per group.

SEATS:
- Scapula-fixed: b1 = r1*sdir(55,15), b2 = r2*sdir(40,95), b3 = r3*sdir(0,95). Each rk = 6 + max over poses of the skin radius along that direction (ray scan with B.dist; expect ~48/62/88 mm).
- Arm-fixed: c1 = armpt(110,-30,R_env+6), c2 = armpt(150,35,R_env+6), c3 = armpt(220,8,R_env+12) (on BOTTOM).

PER POSE:
- Bk = Rs@bk, Ck = Rh@ck, Lk = |Ck-Bk|.
- Moment vectors mk = Ck x (Ck-Bk)/Lk.
- Not taken if |det[m1 m2 m3]| / (|m1||m2||m3|) < 0.15 (near-singular).
- Not taken if any Lk is outside [Lmin_k, 1.9*Lmin_k], where Lmin_k = min over the clip frames - 5 mm (telescope ratio).

METAL:
- Each strut: segment Bk->Ck sampled every 2 mm along the tube; for each sample, offset 4 mm (tube radius) toward the nearest skin point to get the skin-facing surface.
- U-joint blocks: 12 mm cubes at both ends (8 corner/face samples each).
- Report the length-range table.
Contact from the bench.
sweep_params: Scapular seats (acromion lateral/medial, posterior-superior lat 25-55, posterior lat -15..15, lon 80-130). Arm seats (s 90-240, th -45..45; BOTTOM-mounted or cuff-mounted). Strut stand-off 4-10 mm. Singular threshold. Telescope ratio 1.6-2.2.
prior_art: CAREX, a cable-driven arm exoskeleton relying on the human joints (Mao & Agrawal 2012); 3-UPS/3-UPU rehabilitation shoulder mechanisms about a passive spherical joint; self-aligning designs that let the human joint define the centre (Schiele & van der Helm 2006).

name: Fraction pauldron: graded telescoping lames on a gimbal (each lame turns a fixed fraction of the outer angle, rolling-cage coupled), J2 hub, twist on a cuff arc rail
lens: proximity-atlas
family: graded lames / distributed fraction
topology: scapula plate S -> N-1 lames telescoping on circular tracks about one scapula-fixed axis x through GH (lame k at a fixed fraction g_k of the outer angle alpha; rollers on lame k roll between lames k-1 and k+1, bearing-cage principle) -> tip lame T (g=1) -> J2: O20 hub about z (perpendicular to x, carried by T) -> arm strap A -> J3: carriage on a humerus-fixed thin-section arc rail around the upper arm (cone gamma about the humerus axis) -> K7 neck to BOTTOM
dof_reasoning: alpha (the telescope total), beta (J2) and psi (the cuff arc) are the arm's 3 rotations (Fick/Cardan angles about x, then the remaining twist about the humerus axis). Every lame turns about the same axis x, so a rolling cage between k-1 and k+1 fixes k at a weighted mean of its neighbours exactly (holonomic, coaxial rotations commute): the N-1 lame positions are determined by closure, nothing sags unpowered; no gears, pulleys or cables.
description: The proximity atlas says the cap skin moves with graded fractions of the arm swing (~0.1 over the top, ~0.8 over the deltoid). This is the realisable form of that idea: only fractions of ONE angle about ONE axis can be coupled exactly with 1-D elements, so the gimbal's outer angle is spread over telescoping lames like a lobster-tail pauldron.
model_spec: docs/concepts/models/fraction-pauldron.py (concept kit: K3 march, continuity_dense, K6 collisions, K7 neck); lames one radius per across-column (they slide along their whole length), each stacked t + 0.6 mm on the one below; rail constant radius along its length.
sweep_params: x (axis lat/lon), n (lames), fraction exponent, side, stroke coverage cov, rail coverage rcov, profile quantile q, rail cone gamma, width w, overlap ov

name: Spherical 3R on fold-frontier axes
topology:
- Scapula base (S) on the user's scapula handler.
- J1 ACTIVE: O20 hub (preloaded MR117-2RS pair, 12.25 mm stack), axis b = bvec(az, el) through GH.
- Link 1: 12 x 3 mm strap on the great circle J1 -> J2 (arc a1).
- J2 ACTIVE: O20 hub, axis through GH (two-circle closure, branch sigma).
- Link 2: 12 x 3 mm strap J2 -> J3 (arc a2), passing over link 1 and the neck.
- J3 ACTIVE: O20 hub, axis W = wdir(wd, wa) fixed in the humerus.
- Arm-end plate + 14 x 6 neck rigid to BOTTOM's bar (member 3). No cuff slide.
dof_reasoning: Three revolute pins whose axes meet at GH: a spherical chain whose end orientation is the arm's, solved by the two-circle closure (no spare coordinate). The bench's arm rotates about a fixed GH in the scapula frame, so no translation has to be absorbed: 0 passive translations, no cuff slide, 0 mm liner compliance claimed.
description: The plain spherical 3R with its axes re-seeded from the fold frontier (tools/fold_frontier.py, docs/research/fold/frontier.json): the (J1, J3, a1, a2) layouts that keep the J1-J3 axis angle inside the closure band for 85-97 % of the bench workspace at orientation level. Rest / overhead / across: as any spherical 3R; the frontier layouts put J1 anterolateral and nearly horizontal (front of the acromion) and J3 roughly radial on the lateral arm.
why_better: The most buildable chain there is: three pins on bearing pairs, no rail, no slide, no carriage. If the fold frontier's reach (0.94-0.97 at orientation level) survived the skin, it would remove the leaders' main limiter (J2 fold: osn reach 0.706, champion 0.775).
main_risk: Proximity: a scapula-fixed hub on a near-horizontal anterolateral ray sits over the anterior deltoid / humeral head, which moves under it; short arcs make the links sweep over the neck and chest.
unpowered_and_mvp2: Unpowered: three O20 bearing hubs (MR117-2RS pairs) with the user's rotation sensing. MVP2: a drum on each hub, remote motors on cables.
model_spec: docs/concepts/models/fold-sph3r.py (= docs/concepts/models/_template.py build() + crown/wall skin check, near-touch and overhead reports)
sweep_params:
- frontier.json layouts a1 + a2 85-140 (396) x sigma +-1.
- q 0.95 / 0.97, strap width 10 on the top 20.
- CMA-ES: az, el, a1, a2, wd, wa (+ q in one stream), margin 10, width 12.
prior_art: The spherical 3R shoulder exoskeleton (e.g. the concurrent-axis shoulder chains of MGA, ARMin, the project's own champion); new here: the axis layout taken from the measured fold frontier.
lens: fold-frontier
family: spherical 3R

name: Leader 3R closed by a flat two-pin knee instead of the crossed cuff slides (0 passive translations; merged with skin-normal-3r-pinned-cufflink, whitworth-j3-cuff kept as the 1-slider fallback)
family: offset 3R, exact 2-slide subfamily, planar revolute closure
lens: round3:self-alignment / loop closure through cheap rotational passive joints
description: offset-skin-normal-3r (k4216) with its arm end rebuilt. J1 and J2 are O20 hubs on GH rays (acromion top, posterior acromion); J3 is an O20 hub on the lateral deltoid with its axis tilted b3 toward the skin normal so its line misses GH by 7 mm (b3 0.23) to 19 mm (b3 0.6). The 2 crossed RSR3M guides, carriage A, strip, carriage B and bridge are gone. Hub 3's rotor carries a flat Ti arm (E) to pin a; a flat Ti link runs from pin a to pin b on an arm pad fixed to the user's cuff/BOTTOM. Both pins are parallel to J3 and lie in hub 3's plane, tangent to the lateral arm. Rest: the knee lies flat at ~90 deg below hub 3. Overhead / across the body / behind the back the J3 line drift (11.6 x 14.1 mm at k4216, all in hub 3's plane) opens and closes the knee (77-105 deg with E 45 / link 30; 55-140 deg with 20 / 20); nothing stands up.
topology: scapula (user's handler) -> J1 ACTIVE R (axis on a GH ray) -> L1 -> J2 ACTIVE R (axis on a GH ray) -> L2 -> J3 ACTIVE R (axis d3 tilted b3, line offset d from GH) -> E arm -> pin a PASSIVE R (parallel to d3) -> knee link -> pin b PASSIVE R (parallel to d3) -> arm pad on BOTTOM/cuff -> humerus; the loop closes through the wearer's GH. Mobility: q1, q2 set by pointing d3 (spherical IK); the relative motion link 2 -> arm is a pure rotation about the GH line parallel to d3 (the 2-slide closure theorem), i.e. planar; the planar RRR (J3, a, b) has exactly 3 planar DOF, so q3, qa, qb are set by a closed-form two-circle closure. Spatial Grubler gives 2 because of one redundant (d3-normal) constraint, which is identically 0.000 mm in this subfamily; manufacturing error and the radial part of the real GH translation go to the cuff liner (<= 3 mm, stated, as in osn). No undetermined coordinate (R17).
components: J1-J3: v5 O20 hubs, MR117-2RS (7x11x3) back-to-back pair, 12.25 mm F->crown incl. magnet/encoder (docs/HARDWARE.md). Pins a, b: IGLIDUR-PIN (tools/hardware_catalogue.json: iglidur GSM sleeve + 2 GTM thrust washers on an integral O4 Ti pin, 4.5-5 mm over two 2-2.5 mm plates, O10-12 boss) or an MR63ZZ (3x6x2.5) pair, ~6 mm, MVP1 only. E arm 8 x 3 Ti-6Al-4V strap 20-55 mm, knee link 8 x 3 (or 10 x 2.2) Ti 15-35 mm between pins, arm pad O12 x 3 Ti on M2 screws into BOTTOM. Replaces 2x THK RSR3M crossed + adapter (10.5 mm stack, ~10 g). Fallback with the same closure: whitworth-j3-cuff (crank + MR63ZZ pin + ONE RSR3M along the humerus, 9 mm stack, 1 passive translation) - strictly dominated unless the pins fail the MVP2 out-of-plane moment.
dof_reasoning: 3 active (J1-J3); 2 passive pins whose angles come from the two-circle closure; 0 translations. Same loop as osn with the 2 slides replaced by 2 revolutes parallel to J3 (a planar RRR spans the same SE(2) as R + 2P).
model_spec: Stage 0 (done by the round-3 judge): emulation on the leader's own model (scratch knee.py; RAIL_H = CAR_H = h): h 4 -> 32.61 (control reproduced), h 3 -> 30.11, h 2 -> 27.89 on Bench(60,160) fast; Bench(110,360) exact: h 4_4_1 -> 43.36 (reach 0.611, follow 0.964, in-band14 0.779, contact 0.024), h 3_3_1 -> 41.58 (reach 0.614, follow 0.964, in-band14 0.791, contact 0.021), h 2_2_1 -> 39.14 (reach 0.614, follow 0.964, in-band14 0.816, contact 0.021). Stage 1: real knee as a copy of docs/concepts/models/offset-skin-normal-3r.py (keep Design.ik; sv = Q^T t3 is the in-plane drift). Params lE 20-55, lc 15-35, phib, br +-1, pad offset k0. pb = m + lE e_sa + lc (cos phib, sin phib); pa from the two-circle intersection; ok &= |pb - C| in [|lE - lc| + 1, lE + lc - 1], elbow in [30, 150] deg; qa, qb into q for K2 at 10 fps; q3' = q3 + angle(pa - C) - rest. Members: hub-3 disc + E strap (end boss at pad level tr), knee link at tr + the REAL pin stack (4.5-5 iglidur / 6 MR63 pair: use 3.0/3.0-equivalent as the honest default, not 2.0), O12 pad at tr. Delete rail/carA/strip/carB/bridge. Exact-box clearances: link vs hubs 1-3, L1, L2, neck, and E vs pad (1 mm); box_edges contact for the link and both bosses; 2 mm underside samples; jam_contact 1. Stage 2: farm CMA from k4216 and streams D/E/F (sigma 0.3/0.6, 3 streams) over seats, b3 0-0.8 (no travel cap now), lE, lc, phib, br, neck, pin stack {4.5, 6}; convergence gate; then the verifier on Bench(110,360) exact.
sweep_params: seats az1/el1/az2/el2/wd/wa (+-6 deg around k4216 and streams D/E/F), b3 0-0.8, lE 20-55, lc 15-35, phib 0-360, branch +-1, pad offset k0 +-15 mm, pin stack {4.5 iglidur, 6 MR63 pair}, neck 10-20; slim O15 hub 3 (see spine-parked-j2-3r) as a joint lever
main_risk: (0) Exact bench at k4216: honest pin knee 41.58 vs the zero-passive spherical reference 41.73 and osn 43.36 - a tie, so it ranks behind spine-parked-j2-3r unless a b3 > 0.23 re-CMA pays on the exact bench. (1) The honest pin stack is the 3/3 emulation, not 2/2: 30.11 fast (score 89.1), so k4216 alone does not cross 27.5 - it needs the re-CMA and the freed b3. (2) Fast vs exact: osn went 32.61 -> 42.59 on the verifier's Bench(110,360) exact; the exact numbers above are the ones that count. (3) Reach is untouched (0.706 fast / 0.611 exact = 19-29 gap points from the J2 fold) - 90+ on the exact bench needs a fold lever stacked on it. (4) Hub 3 stays 0.495 in band. (5) The swept link (up to 48 x 20 mm) vs neck and hub 3 (R16), the knee near straight (weak MVP2 closure), and pins carrying the cuff's out-of-plane moment.

name: All-skin-normal 3R closed by three pins: a J2 knuckle takes the radial drift, a pinned cuff link the in-plane drift (the buildable form of skin-normal-hubs-selfaligning)
family: offset axes, all-revolute self-alignment
lens: round3:self-alignment / loop closure through cheap rotational passive joints
description: All three O20 hubs sit square on their skin (snh k722 seats: tilts 0.34 / 0.42 / 0.21, lines 5.1 / 6.9 / 6.8 mm off GH). The 3D drift that snh took with a 3-translation stage (refuted: its radial slide would stand ~25 mm) is taken by three pins. (a) Knuckle: link 2 is split 30 mm past hub 2 by a passive pin parallel to J2, flat in hub 2's skin plane; it swings 9..35 deg and supplies the drift along hub 3's normal. (b) Hub 3's 45 mm E arm + a 30 mm cuff link pinned to an arm pad take the in-plane residual (20.6 x 23.0 mm; elbow 68-118 deg). Rest: three flat hubs, two flat straps, one knuckle boss. Overhead / across the body the knuckle folds a few degrees; the radial stroke never appears as height.
topology: scapula -> J1 ACTIVE R (tilted, 5.1 mm off GH) -> L1 -> J2 ACTIVE R (tilted, 6.9 mm off GH) -> crank (30 mm, hub-2 rotor) -> pin k PASSIVE R (parallel to J2) -> L2 -> J3 ACTIVE R (tilted, 6.8 mm off GH) -> E arm (45) -> pin a PASSIVE R (parallel to J3) -> cuff link (30) -> pin b PASSIVE R (parallel to J3) -> arm pad -> humerus (loop closed by GH). Spatial Grubler: 7 bodies, 6 x 1-DOF joints + GH(3): M = 6(7-1-7) + 9 = 3, no redundant constraint. Orientation fixes q1, q2 + qk, q3 + qa + qb; the radial closure fixes qk (one root, authority >= 26.5 mm/rad at p1); the two-circle closure fixes qa, qb. All passive coordinates set by closure (R17).
components: J1-J3: v5 O20 hubs, MR117-2RS (7x11x3) back-to-back pair, 12.25 mm F->crown incl. magnet/encoder (docs/HARDWARE.md). Pins k, a, b: IGLIDUR-PIN (tools/hardware_catalogue.json: iglidur GSM sleeve + 2 GTM thrust washers on an integral O4 Ti pin, 4.5-5 mm over two 2-2.5 mm plates, O10-12 boss) or an MR63ZZ (3x6x2.5) pair, ~6 mm, MVP1 only. Knuckle crank 8 x 3 Ti (first 30 mm of L2, hub-2 upper level), L2b laps over it (+3.15 locally); E arm 8 x 3 x 45 Ti, cuff link 8 x 3 x 42 Ti, arm pad O12 x 3 Ti. No translation part.
dof_reasoning: 3 active + 3 closure-set pins (one radial, two in-plane); generic spatial loop with M = 3 and no redundancy.
model_spec: As the proposal: start from the pin-knee model with b1, b2 > 0; per pose solve (sv + Q^T Delta(qk)) . sn = c0 for qk (0.25 deg grid in [-60, 60] + secant, root nearest the previous 10 fps frame), ok &= root exists, |d/dqk| >= 5 mm/rad, |qk - mid| <= 35 deg; sv' feeds the pinned-cuff triad. Members after the knuckle translated by Delta, L2 split into L2a (crank) and L2b (laps at +3.15); knuckle boss O12; q gets qk, qa, qb. Validation: snh k722 seats vs snh 35.86 (3P, unverified) and the 2P control 45.31. Judge red-team (scratch r3judge/c2c.py, osn Design.ik at snh seats): knuckle root is single-branch and continuous over 350 consecutive fit-clip frame pairs (|dqk| p99 1.5, max 2.0 deg; 0 pairs > 5 deg); swing 9..35 deg, authority p1 26.5 mm/rad, 525 of 576 poses close.
sweep_params: az1, el1, b1 (0-0.6), az2, el2, b2 (0-0.6), wd, wa, b3 (0-0.8), knuckle at J1 or J2, lk 15-35, alk 0-360, c0, lE 25-55, lc 15-35, phib, neck. Seeds: snh k722, osn k4216 with b1 = b2 = 0.3-0.5, fold-frontier configs. Farm CMA 3 streams; verifier Bench(110,360) exact; judge/base_stage.py for R10.
main_risk: (1) The in-band premise (snh chain 0.891) comes from a sweep record that is itself under audit for skin-contoured plates (floating-centre-3r was refuted for that) - the model must use flat straps at their real height. (2) Reach is lower than osn at snh seats (fold-free 0.768 bench, ws 0.681 -> reach ~0.656 = 24 gap fast, worse exact): 90+ needs the fold-frontier seeds or a fold lever. (3) Six joints to sense (twist = q3 + qa + qb, J2 = q2 + qk). (4) The knuckle stack (+3.15 on L2) and the +-6.7 mm tangential shift of hub 3 over the deltoid. (5) Near the fold the radial authority falls; check the 5 mm/rad floor on full 10 fps clips.

name: Closure-set arc knee: hub 3 on a passive trunnion yoke whose tilt changes the J2-J3 arc, set by the radial closure through the wearer's GH (fold lever, rotations only)
family: offset axes + closure-set passive orientation DOF
lens: round3:self-alignment / loop closure through cheap rotational passive joints
description: A skin-normal 3R (snh / osn seats) in which hub 3's housing sits in a fork at the end of link 2 on two trunnion pins, axis dK = u2 x u3 through the hub centre. Tilting the housing by psi changes the J2-J3 arc a2, so the fold window [|a1 - a2| + 10, a1 + a2 - 10] breathes with the pose. psi is set by the radial closure (the one direction the planar cuff pins cannot take); the in-plane drift goes to a pinned cuff link as in skin-normal-3r-pin-knee. Rest: hub level in its fork. Overhead / across the body the closure tilts it (+-31 deg), lifting the rim ~5 mm on one side.
topology: scapula -> J1 ACTIVE R -> L1 -> J2 ACTIVE R -> L2 with fork -> K PASSIVE R (trunnion pair, axis u2 x u3 through hub 3) -> yoke = hub-3 housing -> J3 ACTIVE R (line 6.8 mm off GH) -> E arm -> pin a PASSIVE R -> cuff link -> pin b PASSIVE R -> arm pad -> humerus (closed by GH). M = 6(7-1-7) + 9 = 3. psi fixed by the u3-normal closure equation, qa/qb by the two-circle closure; no spring, no 4th active joint.
components: J1-J3: v5 O20 hubs, MR117-2RS (7x11x3) back-to-back pair, 12.25 mm F->crown incl. magnet/encoder (docs/HARDWARE.md). K: gimbal fork, two coaxial O4 Ti trunnions in IGLIDUR-PIN sleeves or MR63ZZ pairs in 3 mm cheeks (27 mm across the fork; miniature-cardan class, audit row BUILDABLE rotations only). Pins a, b, E arm, cuff link, arm pad as skin-normal-3r-pin-knee.
dof_reasoning: 3 active + trunnion psi + 2 cuff pins, all closure-set; psi is held only by the radial closure (authority p5 10-13 mm/rad, p50 ~29-33 mm/rad).
model_spec: As the proposal (scratch knuckle.py is the prototype): per pose a 1 deg psi grid + secant, root nearest the previous 10 fps frame, ok = root exists & fold-free at psi* & |d radial / d psi| >= 8 mm/rad; hub disc + yoke cheeks get R12 RK(psi*); q gets psi, qa, qb. First run: reproduce 0.832 / 0.836 fold-free-and-closable at hK 75 / 90 on snh seats (judge reproduced both). Then REPORT a continuity-tracked number: the judge's red team (scratch r3judge, root nearest psi=0 per pose as in the prototype) finds 4 of 41 (hK 75) and 3 of 46 (hK 90) consecutive clip-frame pairs whose root jumps 50-55 deg (p50 1 deg) - branch switches the real knee cannot make; the continuity-tracked follow will be below the 0.85 / 0.917 clip share. Then R10: feed judge/base_stage.py's GH-translation sources through the radial closure and report the psi excursion (at p50 authority ~2 deg per mm of radial GH translation, p5 ~5 deg/mm).
sweep_params: dKrot -60..60, hK 70-95, c0, psi limits; az1, el1, b1, az2, el2, b2, wd, wa, b3 0.2-0.6 (raises authority); lE, lc, phib. Seeds: snh k722 (hK 75/90), osn k4216 with b1 = b2 = 0.3-0.5, frontier layouts a1 + a2 85-110. Log fold-free-and-closable (ws, clip) to split the knee's gain from proximity.
main_risk: (1) Branch jumps (measured above): the closure root is not single-valued along the clips, so follow drops. (2) Conditioning: 1 mm liner compression or radial GH translation moves psi 2-5.7 deg; R10's real GH translation (15 mm rigid worst) can swing the knee tens of degrees - judge R10 before L1. (3) Unpowered the knee carries only ~0.05-0.07 N.m before the cuff exceeds 5 N. (4) c0 is tuned on the bench poses (fit); check held-out. (5) +-31 deg tilt lifts the rim ~5 mm; 6 angles to sense. Upper bound if psi were free: fold-free 0.973 vs 0.768 - the largest lever left, if it can be made well-conditioned.

name: Zero-passive spherical 3R at the leader's seats: J2 parked over the posterior acromion, tilted d3, slim O15 J2/J3 hubs (merged with slim-hub-spine-parked-3r and the bench part of tilted-spherical-follower-slide)
family: spherical 3R
lens: round3:zero-passive spherical chain that removes the hub-2-over-deltoid limiter by placement
description: Three hubs, every axis through GH, no stage, no slides. Hub 1 on the acromion top (bvec(96-101, 63-65)), hub 2 behind it over the posterior acromion / scapular spine (branch sigma -1 and a short link 1 keep J2's circle on the posterior-superior cap, so hub 2 never crosses the lateral deltoid), hub 3 on the lateral deltoid with the leader's d3 direction (the d3 'tilt' is a spherical freedom: b3 0 -> 0.23 took the osn reference from 46.71 to 33.40). J2 and J3 are slim O15 hubs (same MR117 pair in a 2 mm Ti wall); J1 stays O20. Arm end: K7 neck to BOTTOM. R10 options judged separately: cuff liner, one RSR3M along the humerus, or the horizontal base follower slide (u = (-0.56, 0.01, 0.83) ISB, 15.2 -> 8.4 mm fit / 6.6 held-out, judge/base_stage.py sources).
topology: scapula handler -> base -> J1 ACTIVE R (through GH) -> link 1 (12x3 Ti) -> J2 ACTIVE R (through GH, sigma -1) -> link 2 (12x3 Ti, over link 1 and the neck) -> J3 ACTIVE R (through GH) -> neck 14x6 -> BOTTOM -> cuff. 0 passive in the chain (optional: 1 base slide for R10, set by a bony follower - outside the bench).
components: J1: v5 O20 hub (MR117-2RS pair, 12.25 mm). J2, J3: slim O15 hub, same MR117-2RS pair in a 2.0 mm Ti wall (O11 + 2 x 2), M14x0.5 cap, O6 x 2.5 magnet over a 1.6 mm PCB, same 12.25 mm stack; conservative fallback O17 (2.75 mm wall). Links Ti 12 x 3 (5.5 for MVP2), neck 7075 14 x 6. Optional R10 base slide: THK RSR3N, rail 43-45 mm, 2 blocks.
dof_reasoning: Pure spherical 3R; no passive coordinate on the bench.
model_spec: Kit model from docs/concepts/models/_template.py, PARAMS az 101.417, el 63.392, a1 41.079, a2 77.120, wd 84.950, wa -16.335, sigma -1, q 0.98 (reproduce kit 44.45; k4216 axes 45.01; slim J2/J3 43.00). Add a declared-component radius to the kit audit (Chain.info['hub_rad'] tied to a new tools/hardware_catalogue.json entry 'MR117-pair-O15-slim'), not force=True. Judge red team: the same morphology scores 33.40 in osn's VModel spherical reference ({'slides': 0}, reproduced by the judge, hub 3 0.225 in band at 17.3 mm median) and 45.01 in the kit at the same axes - a ~12-point model-fidelity split the verifier must settle on Bench(110,360) exact (41.73 (reach 0.617, follow 0.964, in-band14 0.784, contact 0.018) for the VModel version). Report the pose list for the q 0.98 drop (pl-15 el90-105 ax45-60 and clip pl30 el66 ax-43: arm lying on hub 2) and the reach-loss breakdown (noclose / K2 / K6 / contact). CMA: az, el, a1 36-50, a2 68-90, wd, wa, q 0.96-1.0, rad2/rad3 {7.5, 8.5, 10}.
sweep_params: az 85-115, el 55-75, a1 36-50, a2 68-90, wd 70-95, wa -30..0, q 0.96-1.0 (sigma -1), rad2/rad3 in {7.5, 8.5, 10}; fold margin 5-10 as a sensitivity only
main_risk: (0) Ranked 1st by the judge: on Bench(110,360) exact its VModel form (osn slides 0, k4216) scores 41.73, level with or better than every passive arm end measured at the same seats (osn 43.36, honest pin knee 41.58). (1) Reach is capped near 0.61-0.64 by the J2 fold: the short link 1 that parks hub 2 narrows the window. Expected 35-42 after CMA - it does not cross 27.5 alone; its role is the cleanest buildable control (0 passive) that every passive design must beat. (2) q 0.98 turns the arm-over-hub-2 poses into dropped contact poses: a pinch the red team must rule out as non-everyday. (3) The O15 wall (2 mm Ti, M14x0.5 cap thread, ~1.2 mm under the thread root) is MVP1-only; hand calc before credit. (4) R10's ~15 mm goes to the cuff or the base follower; judge R10 before L1.

name: Fold lever on the pin-knee leader: J1 on a passive acromial rocker whose angle the arm sets through an S-U tie rod (rotations only)
family: scheduled 4th axis: spherical/offset 3R + passive base rocker + tie rod
lens: round3:behind / on top of the scapula - a graded-fraction J1 that keeps the J1-J3 angle in the fold window
description: A passive pivot boss on the lateral acromion top (S-quiet skin, 0.95-1.0 in band at 47-50 mm), axis through GH, carries a small rocker plate. One arm holds the J1 hub (axis 14-20 deg from the pivot axis, so J1's line still passes through GH and the pin-knee closure theorem still holds); the other holds a ball stud ~45 deg from the pivot toward the posterior-superior shoulder. A 55-62 mm Ti tie rod joins it to a stud on the arm-end plate by hub 3. Overhead the arm pulls the rod, the rocker turns and J1 precesses on its cone away from J3, widening the fold margin; across the body / behind the back it turns the other way.
topology: scapula -> J0 PASSIVE R (pivot, through GH) -> rocker -> J1 ACTIVE R (through GH) -> link 1 -> J2 ACTIVE R -> link 2 -> J3 ACTIVE R -> pin knee -> arm; tie: rocker stud -> PASSIVE spherical (ball link) -> rod -> PASSIVE U (miniature U-joint) -> arm-end plate. The judge requires S-U, not S-S: an S-S rod has an idle spin about its own axis, an undetermined passive coordinate. q0 has a closed form (q0 = phi + s0 acos x) from the rod length; transmission angle >= 25 deg and |q0| <= 75 deg.
components: J0: MR63ZZ or MR85ZZ pair in a 2 x 2.5 mm plate boss, ~6 mm stack, no encoder (catalogue passive pin; sense it anyway: J1's direction depends on it). J1-J3: v5 O20 hubs. Tie rod O4 x 0.5 Ti tube 55-62 mm; one end an M3 ball link (4.8 mm ball stud, acetal socket ~O8 x 12, or an igus igubal rod end - part number to be confirmed), the other a miniature U-joint (O6-8 needle/pin cardan). Arm end: skin-normal-3r-pin-knee.
dof_reasoning: 3 active; rocker angle set by the rod-length closure; ball (3) + U (2) at the rod ends set by the rod geometry with no idle spin.
model_spec: Kit model docs/concepts/models/acromial-rocker-3r.py from _template.py (proposal's build: c, A0, b0, C; q0 closed form; ok &= |x| <= cos 25 deg and |q0| <= 75 deg; q0 into q for K2 dense; rod as chord points with K3/K6; ball link and U as O8 x 12 boxes). Plain-3R control at the same seats in the same file. Then port onto the pin-knee model (u1 -> rot(c, q0, u1)). Report reach split into fold / rod dead point / contact. Kill test: on the leader's seats the narrow proxy already found no reach gain (0.68-0.78); proceed only if the kit shows reach > 0.75 at <= 2 points of in-band loss.
sweep_params: pivot azc / elc (within 30 deg of J1); J1 cone 8-25 deg; rod stud azA / elA (30-55 deg from the pivot); arm stud dC 85-115 / aC -30..30; rocker cap 45-90 deg; transmission floor 20-30 deg; a1 / a2 / J3 seat; branches
main_risk: No real-skin gain shown: in the proxy the reach gain (+0.03-0.09) is paid back in in-band (net break-even), and the per-point proxy was refuted by the kit at the crest seats. Capping the rocker at +-75 deg may keep little of the fold gain. The rod over the acromion edge is a pinch point overhead; the pivot adds a 6 mm boss under J1; MVP2 rod reaction on the arm.

name: Fold-free spherical 3R whose J2 is a link-1 arc-rail sector with a link-2 roller carriage (no J2 hub; virtual J2 axis)
family: spherical 3R (virtual-axis J2)
lens: round3:J2 as a short curved rail with a real carriage, on a fold-free axis layout
description: Hub 1 on the acromion top (bvec(96, 65)); fold-free arcs a1 60 / a2 80 (kit: closure 0.90, reach 0.82 in the hub version vs 0.706 for the leader). No metal on the J2 axis point (in band 3 %): J2 is a flat Ti arc rail, pitch radius 30 mm about the J2 axis at ~52 mm along it, a 125 deg sector on link 1's end on the J1 side; a 4-V-roller carriage fixed to link 2 at chi +90 deg rides it (psi -46..+58 deg p2-p98). Link 2 runs from the carriage to the O20 J3 hub on the lateral deltoid, then the K7 neck.
topology: scapula handler -> base -> J1 ACTIVE R (through GH, O20) -> link 1 with arc-rail sector -> J2 ACTIVE R about a virtual axis through GH (circular rail + roller carriage) -> link 2 -> J3 ACTIVE R (through GH, O20) -> K7 neck -> BOTTOM -> cuff. The rollers are the active joint's bearing; 0 passive DOF.
components: J2: custom Ti-6Al-4V flat arc rail 8 x 4 with ground 90 deg V edges, R 30 mm, ~90 mm of arc (constant section swept along an arc - no loft); carriage Ti 12 x 12 x 3 with 4x MR63ZZ V-rollers on M3 shoulder pins (2 eccentric), ~8-9 mm over the rail underside; J2 sensing by a multipole strip + hall sensor in the carriage; machined end stops. J1, J3: v5 O20 hubs. Links Ti 12 x 3, neck 7075 14 x 6.
dof_reasoning: Pure spherical 3R; J2 realised by a guided arc, its coordinate is the active J2 angle.
model_spec: Kit model from _template.py as the proposal (rail and carriage as pose-local 'flat' members, 2 mm grid; Chain.hubless = ('J2',)). First run az 95.8565, el 65.2093, a1 60, a2 80, wd 79.148, wa -13.3653, R 30, psi -50..58, q 0.98; the kit must confirm rail 0.95-0.99, carriage 0.97, link 1 0.98 in band (centre-ray claims). Then the link-2-frame ceiling map and a two-segment planform-turn link 2 through its best cells (no loft). Controls in the same file: hub version at identical axes (73.57) and spine-parked-j2-3r. Kill if link 2 cannot be routed above 0.6 in band.
main_risk: (1) Link 2 is the unsolved limiter: 0.10-0.71 in band along its great circle (frame set by closure, as the champion's link 2 at ceiling 0.04). (2) Rail ends: travel plus the carriage half-length reaches the in-band sector's edge; end stops cost ~2-4 % of poses. (3) A cantilevered custom V-arc with eccentric preload: play, stiffness and arc sensing less mature than a hub encoder. (4) Close to rail-elbow (dead, refuted by its own 3R control): the hub control at identical axes is mandatory.

name: Raglan-routed 3R (plain spherical 3R whose links follow the lines of least skin motion, measured in each link's frame)
topology: S -> J1: ACTIVE R (O20 hub, axis through GH) -> link 1 (8 x 3 strap with ONE planform turn fixed in the link: hub -> W -> hub, W = cos(d) slerp(h1, h2, t) + sin(d) n_12) -> J2: ACTIVE R (O20 hub, axis through GH) -> link 2 (same, its own turn) -> J3: ACTIVE R (O20 hub, axis through GH) -> arm-end plate + K7 neck rigid to BOTTOM's bar. Each hub may sit at either end of its axis line (e1, e2, e3).
dof_reasoning: Spherical 3R: the three axis directions meet at GH; the exact closure (concept_kit.closure) sets J2 from J1 and J3, so every coordinate is set by the arm (no slide, no undetermined coordinate). The planform turn and the hub-end choice change only the link shapes, not the kinematics.
description: A pattern maker's answer to the 3R's floating links: draft each link along the measured line where the skin keeps one distance from THAT link over every pose (raglan map: the K3 requirement on a (t, d) grid of the link's own moving frame), with one planform turn (constant section, tangent-arc corner, no loft). Plus a grading pass over the whole layout space (three-hub band scan) for layouts where all three hubs can be pinned in one 12 mm band. REST: hub 1 on top of the shoulder, hub 2 behind it, hub 3 on the lateral arm; link 1 bows out over the posterior deltoid instead of dropping straight down the back. OVERHEAD / ACROSS / BEHIND: as the plain 3R (same kinematics), the bowed link keeps its skin distance where the straight one crossed the acromion edge.
why_better: Link 1 in band 0.37 -> 0.60 at the plain-3R basin, gap 51.33 -> 42.72 (Bench(60,160) fast) with 0 passive translations: the most buildable morphology (3 pins + 2 bent straps).
main_risk: Hub 2 floats (F 128-145 mm) in every plain-3R basin with good reach: link 2 and hub 2 stay out of band; the graded family that pins hub 2 (F 65) loses reach to the fold and needs a 100 deg link 2 down the deltoid.
unpowered_and_mvp2: Unpowered: three pins on MR117-2RS pairs, links machined or bent from 8 x 3 Ti (or Al 7075) strap; MVP2: remote motors on the three hubs (cables), as the spherical 3R.
model_spec: docs/concepts/models/raglan-routed-3r.py on tools/concept_kit.py (K0-K7) + fold-sph3r crown / near-touch / overhead checks; routed_strap() = two (or three) strap_dirs legs concatenated into one Member with one climb-limited grid; map mode = the raglan map; tools/hub_band_scan.py = the grading scan.
sweep_params: az, el (J1 bvec), a1, a2, wd, wa (J3 wdir), sigma, e1-e3 (hub ends), r1t, r1d, r2t, r2d (+ r1t2, r1d2, r2t2, r2d2: a second turn), width >= 8, q
prior_art: Raglan / princess seams (tailoring); Iberall 1964 lines of non-extension, MIT BioSuit (Newman); orthotic casting in functional positions and trim lines on stable landmarks; spherical 3R shoulder exoskeletons (e.g. Harmony, ABLE) route links on great circles.
source: round 3, tailoring / pattern-making / orthotic fitting lens

name: Far-end posterior 3R (fold-free posterior J1 line, hubs at either end of their axis lines, raglan-routed links)
topology: S -> J1: ACTIVE R (O20 hub on the posterior-horizontal GH line bvec(-24, 4), at either end) -> routed link 1 -> J2: ACTIVE R (hub at either end of its GH line) -> routed link 2 -> J3: ACTIVE R (posterior arm wdir(80, -90), or its far end) -> neck to BOTTOM.
dof_reasoning: Spherical 3R (exact closure); the hub end changes no kinematics.
description: The far-end scan found a fold-free J1 line (straight back from GH, horizontal) whose hub stays in one band in 100 % of poses; this morphology builds the 3R on it with every hub-end choice and routed links.
why_better: Fold-free on 100 % of poses (orientation level).
main_risk: Measured, fatal: the fold-free arcs send link rays through the neck / chest in 10-20 % of poses (links park at 400 mm) and every far end of a GH line lies in the torso, axilla or neck.
unpowered_and_mvp2: as raglan-routed-3r
model_spec: docs/concepts/models/far-end-posterior-3r.py (the raglan-routed-3r builder, posterior layout)
sweep_params: 4 fold-free posterior layouts x branch x e1-e3 x route x q

name: Fold-free human-closed 3-RUS truss: three scapula crank hubs, O5 rods to arm ball studs, the user's GH closes the loop
topology:
- Scapula base (S) on the user's scapula handler: three O20 crank hubs on GH rays (ACTIVE revolutes) joined by 12 x 3 base brackets.
- Each hub carries a crank of arc beta_k (12 x 3 Ti strap); at its tip an O12 U-joint (passive, 2 rot).
- O5 Ti rod (rigid, its bow fitted) to an O12 rod end on a ball stud (passive, 3 rot) on a 14 x 4 arm saddle at the humeral-head level.
- No exo joint at GH: the user's glenohumeral joint closes all three loops.
dof_reasoning: Grubler-Kutzbach on the bench (GH fixed in S): 3 legs x (R 1 + U 2 + S 3) + GH 3 = 21 joint freedoms - 3 loops x 6 = 3; the 3 rod spins are killed by the U pitch pins; the 3 crank angles are the only coordinates (closed-form RUS IK, branch fixed per leg); numeric rank check = |det| of the three unit moment lines T_k x Q_k >= 0.10. 0 passive translations; all passive freedoms are rotations of catalogue parts (U-joints, rod ends).
description: Leg-fold theorem: each RUS leg closed by GH is a spherical RRR with its OWN fold band angle(c_k, Q_k) in [|beta_k - gamma_k|, beta_k + gamma_k]; the truss gives three independently placed bands instead of the 3R's one, seeded from the fold-free (c, q) pairs of docs/research/fold/ends.json (posterior-horizontal crank axis + posterior humeral-head stud: fold-free at 65 / 65).
why_better: A fold lever made only of rotations: the 3R's single J1-J3 band is replaced by three per-leg bands each placed outside the workspace; no J2 hub on a moving GH ray.
main_risk: Crank parking (a 60-85 deg crank circle sweeps the arm / trunk), the parallel singularity with clustered studs, and ~15 fitted rigid parts on one shoulder.
unpowered_and_mvp2: Unpowered: three O20 bearing hubs with the user's rotation sensing (crank angles map 1:1 to the arm's rotation on a fixed GH; GH translation reads as ~2-3 deg per 3 mm). MVP2: three remote motors on the scapula base; the net rod force Sigma F_k loads the humeral head (a 3R reacts it through its base).
model_spec: docs/concepts/models/foldfree-rus-truss.py (patch-on-load of docs/concepts/models/human-closed-crank-rods.py: options studs3, crank_over; bench_eval / evaluate (flat, CMA) / frozen + wear (near-touch, overhead, red team))
sweep_params: seats from ends.json fold-free lines and the dome; studs s 0-160 mm, theta -60..150; beta 35-85; branch per leg; p 90-100; crank_over

name: Coaxial RUS turret: three stacked crank bearings on one posterior scapula seat, O5 rods to arm studs, the user's GH closes the loop
topology:
- One O20 hub shaft on the fold-free posterior-horizontal scapula seat carrying three crank layers (each on its own thin-section bearing, 4.5 mm per layer, stack 21.25 mm): the three ACTIVE crank axes coincide.
- Each crank: arc beta_k, O12 U-joint at the tip, O5 rod to an O12 rod end on a ball stud on the arm saddle.
- The user's GH closes the loops; no base brackets.
dof_reasoning: As foldfree-rus-truss (Grubler 21 - 18 = 3 on the bench; rod spins killed by the U pitch pins); coaxial cranks keep full rank iff the moment lines T_k x Q_k span 3-space (det >= 0.10 checked per pose). 0 passive translations.
description: Coaxial-input spherical parallel mechanism worn on the user (the humerus is the platform, GH its centre), all three legs on the single seat that is fold-free with many studs.
why_better: One hub footprint on the quietest scapula skin, no base brackets, MVP2 motors on one axis (one cable bundle), unlimited common rotation.

name: Raglan-knee 3R (pin-knee leader with links bent along the lines of least skin motion)
topology: S -> J1: ACTIVE R (O20 hub on a GH ray) -> link 1 (8 x 3 Ti bent bar: two straight legs + ONE tangent arc in the planform, fixed in the link) -> J2: ACTIVE R (O20 hub on a GH ray) -> link 2 (same, its own turn) -> J3: ACTIVE R (offset skin-normal O20 hub on the deltoid) -> E strap -> pin a -> knee link -> pin b -> arm pad on BOTTOM's cuff (flat two-pin knee, 5 mm iglidur pin stack).
dof_reasoning: The pin knee's chain: J1 / J2 on GH rays make the arm-vs-member-3 drift planar in hub 3's plane, and the closed planar RRR knee (two passive pins) absorbs it; every coordinate is set by the arm (closed-form IK + two-circle knee closure). The planform turns change only the link shapes, not the kinematics. Passive translations 0.
description: The tailor's raglan seam applied to the best buildable design: measure, in each link's own moving frame, the sphere-traced need of every direction over every pose the chain takes (raglan map), and bend the link along the best line (one planform turn, constant 8 x 3 section, tangent-arc corner, no loft); then let CMA move the seats with the routes, and try the posterior J1 line (the far-end scan's fold-free lead) in this family.
why_better: Measured: at the leader seats the raglan map's argmax is the great circle (routes only: +0.45 real, the rest in-band dilution); CMA over seats + routes: 23.00 fast (23.62 at fixed part sizes) and 31.52 frozen Bench(110,360) exact vs the pin knee's 26.34 / 33.84 - mostly a J3 seat move (hub 3 / knee into band), +0.9 from the bent link 1.
main_risk: The leader's CMA already put both links on their raglan lines (the map's argmax is the great circle); the limiter is the J2 fold (reach), which no routing touches.
unpowered_and_mvp2: Unpowered: three MR117-2RS hubs, two iglidur knee pins, two bent 8 x 3 Ti bars; MVP2: remote motors on the three hubs (cables).
model_spec: docs/concepts/models/raglan-knee-3r.py: a private import of skin-normal-3r-pin-knee.py with S.Geometry.add_links replaced by the routed path (great-circle legs + tangent arc, resampled at 2 mm, 4 sample rows); `map` mode = the raglan map; `frozen` = the pin knee's frozen protocol.

name: Stop-relay rocker 3R: J1 rides a spring-centred acromial rocker that only moves once J2 is on a hard stop 10 deg short of its fold
family: scheduled 4th axis: spherical 3R + passive base rocker (force-closed by stops and a centring spring)
topology: scapula (handler) -> R0 PASSIVE (pivot, axis c through GH, spring-centred, |q0| <= 75, sensed) -> rocker plate -> J1 ACTIVE R (axis u1 through GH, O20) -> link 1 -> J2 ACTIVE R (O15, hard stops at q2 = -34.1 / -137.4) -> link 2 -> J3 ACTIVE R (O15, arm-fixed axis) -> K7 neck -> BOTTOM -> cuff
description:
At rest it looks exactly like the verified leader spine-parked-j2-3r (CMA-B / k7008 seats): J1 on the acromion top, J2 parked over the posterior acromion, J3 on the lateral deltoid, 12x3 Ti straps. The difference is under hub 1. A small slim pivot hub (O15) sits on the acromion / AC top, 30 deg from J1 (about 31 mm at the hub radius), with its axis through GH at bvec(-159.9, 75.4). A 30-deg Ti rocker plate carries hub 1 from that pivot, and two opposed preloaded torsion springs centre it. Hub 2 has two hard stops at the leader's own jam margins, q2 = -34.1 deg (theta = angle(J1, J3) = 43.1) and q2 = -137.4 deg (theta = 104.4).

Mode A (every fit clip, and 0.639 of the big-bench workspace): the rocker sits on its centre and the chain is the leader, metal for metal. Overhead flexion and abduction past the folded margin (theta < 43.1): J2 reaches its stop before the fold, the arm keeps pushing, and the rocker breaks away against the spring, so J1 precesses on its 30-deg cone over the acromion top (q0 up to about +-60 deg). Across the body / extended (theta > 104.4): the same happens on the other stop, which recovers only 1-2 poses. Behind the back: mode A. All extra metal (pivot, rocker strap) stays on S-quiet skin: pivot 0.98-1.0 in band, rocker strap 0.99.
components: Pivot R0: MR117-2RS pair (7x11x3) in the declared O15 slim housing (2.0 mm Ti wall, 12.25 mm stack incl. an AS5600 + O6x2.5 magnet; the rocker angle must be read in modes B/C). Centring: two opposed preloaded torsion springs (stock music-wire torsion springs, e.g. Lee Spring / Gutekunst T-series, wire 1.2-1.4 mm, mean diameter about 12-14 mm, legs on a centre pin), T0 about 0.2 N.m breakaway each side, about 0.35 N.m at 60 deg. Stress check: d 1.4 mm gives about 1.8 GPa at 60 deg, so R9 must confirm, or use a V-cam + Misumi spring-plunger centring detent (constant about 0.28 N.m). Rocker: 12x3 Ti-6Al-4V strap on a 30-deg great circle; it is hub 1's lower member, so hub 1 rises by one STACK (3.15 mm). J1: v5 O20 hub (MR117 pair). J2: O15 slim hub plus a hard stop: an O2 dowel on the upper member running in a 103-deg arc slot of the lower member, with PEEK / iglidur faces. J3: O15 slim hub. Links: 12x3 Ti straps. No slides, no gears, pulleys or cables.
why_better:
The measured limiter of the leader is the J2 fold: 130 of 360 big-bench workspace poses lie outside theta in [43.1, 104.4], and overhead reach is 5-7 of 28. Measured here on the raw bench frames at the leader seats (az 102.78, el 65.35, a1 40.68, a2 73.76, wd 84.49, wa -12.76, sigma -1).

Kinematics:
- Bench(110,360) workspace inside a fold-free mode rises from 0.639 to 0.775.
- Overhead (elevation >= 140) rises from 0.357 to 0.571.
- Clips stay at 1.000 (their theta 45.7-100.1 never leaves mode A, so follow is untouched).
- Bench(60,160): closing 0.795 -> 0.850 (workspace 0.719 -> 0.794); 11 poses in mode C, 1 in mode B; q0 used -49.7..+58.9 deg.

Proximity (axis-ray and strap-centreline proxy, per-member level = q 0.98 quantile, 12-mm window):
- In-band proxy 0.922 against the leader's 0.924 under the same instrument.
- Per member: pivot 0.979, hub 1 0.984, hub 2 0.973, hub 3 0.706, rocker 0.995, link 1 0.983, link 2 0.862.
- So the reach comes almost free in band.

Estimated gap (proxy, big-bench kinematics x 0.93, in-band - 0.05 calibration): 20.7 against the leader's 32.9 on the same proxy. The leader is verified at 34.29 frozen exact, so expect about 21-24 frozen exact (score about 91-92).

Why it is honest:
- The coordinate is set by a unilateral stop plus a centring spring.
- For a given pose, the energy minimum is the closure root with the least |q0| and J2 on its stop. That root is unique within +-75 deg.
- At the switch the mode-B/C 3R (c, u1, u3), with arcs (30, 43.1 or 104.4), has >= 10 deg margin (checked: stop_ok), so the singular pass happens 10 deg before the fold, never at it.
- Gravity of the chain about c (about 80 g x 50 mm = 0.04 N.m) plus J1 friction (<= 0.07 N.m) is below T0 = 0.2 N.m, so mode A cannot sag.
- With J1, J2 and J3 frictionless, the chain carries no moment about any GH axis, so cuff loads do not trip the rocker.

Complexity about 13.5: passive rotation 2, sensed passive 5, spring 3, body + joint 2, parts about 1.5. That is 12.6 estimated gap points bought for 13.5 complexity points.

Variants measured:
- beta 40, phi 345: big 0.803, in-band 0.900 (hub 2 drops to 0.36).
- beta 25, phi 345: big 0.753, in-band 0.922.
main_risk:
1. R17 / dynamics: the switch is a force-closed relay, not a kinematic one.
   - Bearing friction or chain inertia above T0 could trip the rocker early in mode A.
   - Friction could leave hysteresis or chatter at the switch.
   - The wearer feels up to about 0.35 N.m while the rocker is out. It must be run in judge/dynamics.py with the stop and spring modelled.
2. The fit clips never cross the switch. Every gained pose is a workspace pose, so the 10 fps continuity check does not exercise the relay. Build a synthetic overhead-flexion clip.
3. MVP2: in modes B/C, J2 sits on its stop and the rocker is unactuated. Overhead assistance then needs a 4th motor or stays passive.
4. The torsion-spring stress at d 1.4 mm is at the music-wire limit. A V-cam + spring-plunger detent is the fallback.
5. Hub 1 rides one layer higher on the rocker (+3.15 mm). That is not in the proxy.

expected_gap: proxy 20.7 (leader 32.9 on the same proxy); expected 21-24 on Bench(110,360) frozen exact (leader verified 34.29); crosses 27.5 if the kit confirms the in-band

name: Dwell four-bar knee (Watt six-bar) 3R: a crank-rocker loop between link 1 and a split link 2 shortens link 2 only near the folded side, with pins only and no spring
family: spherical 3R with a polycentric (Watt six-bar) middle joint; all axes through GH
topology: scapula -> J1 ACTIVE R (O20) -> link 1 (carries J2 and pin P) -> J2 ACTIVE R (O15, sensed) -> L2a (40 deg) -> knee K PASSIVE R -> L2b (carries Q and J3) -> J3 ACTIVE R (O15) -> K7 neck -> BOTTOM; loop closure: link 1 -> P PASSIVE R -> rocker C (44.6 deg) -> Q PASSIVE R -> L2b. All axes through GH; spherical Gruebler: 6 bodies, 6 revolutes, M = 3(6 - 1) - 2*6 = 3.
description:
This is the leader's chain with link 2 split at a knee 40 deg from J2 (on the J2-J3 great circle, chi about 0) and closed by a short rocker.

Parts of the loop:
- Pin P sits on link 1, 17.8 deg from J2, over the posterior acromion.
- Pin Q sits on L2b, 15 deg from the knee.
- A 44.6-deg rocker strap C joins P to Q.

How it moves:
- Over the leader's working range the loop sits near its dwell: the knee stays within a few deg of straight, so a2_eff stays about 73.7, which is the leader.
- As J2 folds toward the leader's folded margin, the loop pulls the knee in, and a2_eff shortens to 61.0. The fold therefore moves from theta 43.1 to 23.1.
- The knee angle is a fixed function of q2, so all three encoders stay J1-J3 and MVP2 still drives everything with 3 motors.

Where the metal sits:
- P, the rocker and hub 2 sit on the posterior acromion (0.96-0.98 in band).
- The knee and Q sit at the deltoid edge.
- Q is the weak pin: three posterior-axillary-fold poses (#93, #92, #115: ABER behind the frontal plane, the leader's own pinch poses) lift the skin under it to 110-123 mm.
components: J1: v5 O20 hub, MR117-2RS pair. J2 and J3: O15 slim hubs, MR117-2RS pair. K, P and Q: passive pins with no encoder, each an MR63ZZ pair (3x6x2.5) in an O10 Ti boss on two 2.5-3 mm plates, about a 6.5 mm stack (catalogue: passive pin). Links: 12x3 Ti straps. Rocker C: an 8x3 Ti strap, two-force member, 44.6 deg. L2b: a small triangular 3 mm Ti plate K-Q, plus the strap to J3. No springs, slides, gears, pulleys or cables.
why_better:
The virtual-pole-4bar-j2 track measured that compact four-bars only SHIFT the window. This one is a crank-rocker run near its dwell, and it reshapes the curve of u3 in link 1's frame: a2_eff falls from 73.7 to 61.0 only at the folded side.

Kinematics (k21: b 40.1, chi -0.5, P at arc 17.8 / az 14.5 from J2 in link 1's frame (J1 at az 0), Q at arc 15 from K, 152.8 deg off the K-J3 direction, rocker 44.6 deg, rest at crank 188; monotone segment crank 181-321):
- Fold-free window [23.1, 104.3] with a conservative 10-deg margin at both ends.
- Transmission at Q 45.8-134.6 deg, at K 26-92 deg.
- Bench(110,360) workspace 0.778 against the leader's 0.639; Bench(60,160) 0.794 against 0.719; clips 1.0.

Proximity (same axis-ray / centreline proxy, q 0.98):
- In-band 0.909 against the leader's 0.924.
- Per member: hub 1 0.995, hub 2 0.947, P 0.979, K 0.877, Q 0.016, hub 3 0.701, link 1 0.976, J2-P plate 0.967, L2a 0.973, rocker 0.973, L2b 0.84 / 0.84.
- Q with an O10 boss at q 0.95: 0.66 in band.

Estimated gap 21.8 against the leader's 32.9 on the same proxy. The other basins found: k23 at 23.5 (window [21.1, 100.3]) and k22 at 30.7.

An unconstrained four-bar search shows why the geometry must be seeded on the leader. 3 seeds x 6000 random four-bars with free arcs reach big-bench kinematic 0.958 (window [11, 149]), but hub 2 wanders: 0.02 in band, best proxy 44.8. Seeded on the leader's link 2 (fb2.curve), 3 x 1000 s of hill climbing found the dwell solution.

A DP over hub 2's azimuth about J1 shows the limit: hub 2 alone can stay in band (0.96-0.98) over theta 10-150 only if a2_eff runs from 22 up to 108 or more (J2 kept near the J1-J3 arc). A full-range morphing link is therefore not wearable, and the folded-side dwell is the wearable part.

A dwell CAM in place of the rocker (knee = -3 deg per deg of q2 past the margin) gives only [32.7, 104.4]: big 0.703, proxy 27.8. The rocker loop beats a realistic cam ratio.

Complexity about 17: 3 passive rotations 6, 1 loop 4, 2 bodies 2, 3 joints 3, parts about 2. That is about 3.5 points more than the relays, but with no spring, no sensed passive, and MVP2 kept at 3 motors.
main_risk:
1. Pin Q: the posterior axillary fold (poses #93 / #92 / #115) parks it high. It must be moved, or those poses dropped by q, at some in-band cost.
2. Four pins plus a rocker within 20-45 deg of each other near J2 and the knee is a stacking problem: rocker vs L2a vs link 1 layers. The proxy has no K6.
3. Spread is loop-tolerance sensitive: the three pins must meet at GH within about 0.5 deg, or the loop binds (R17).
4. The search is not converged: 3 local streams, top-3 spread 9 gest.
model_spec:
Subclass the spine-parked-j2-3r model. Precompute the loop in link 1's frame once per build on a 0.25-deg crank grid s:
1. u2 = z, u1 = sdir(a1, 0), J30 = sdir(a2, 0), K0 = knee_of(z, J30, b, chi), Q0 = knee_of(K0, J30, k, alq), P = sdir(gP, phP).
2. Rocker arc r = angle(P, Rz(sref) Q0).
3. Per s: Ks = Rz(s) K0; Qs = K.closure(P, Ks, r, k, sgn, 0), with sgn the branch holding Q0 at sref; u3(s) from J30's coordinates in the (K0, tangent(K0 -> Q0), normal) frame, re-expressed in the (Ks, Qs) frame; th(s) = angle(u1, u3(s)).
4. ok(s) = Q exists and the transmission angles hold: at Q (K-Q-P) in [30, 150], at K (J2-K-Q) in [20, 160].
5. Take the monotone valid segment that contains the leader's half-turn; the window is [th_min + 10, th_max - 10].

Per pose: th = angle(F.S(bvec), F.HG(wdir)); s = interpolation of th(s) on the segment. R maps (u1, u3(s)) to the world pair (p1, p3) with frame(a, b) = [a, unit(b - (a.b) a), a x that]. World axes: p2 = R z, K = R Ks, P = R P, Q = R Qs. q = [q1, s, psi, q3] in dense continuity.

Members:
- hub1 (rad 10), hub2 (7.5), hub3 (7.5);
- pins P, K, Q as flat hub members, rad 5, t = 6.5 (declared MR63 boss; the kit audit needs a declared-radius path like SLIM);
- straps link1 (J1 -> J2), plate J2 -> P, L2a (J2 -> K), rocker C (P -> Q, 8 mm wide, its own layer), L2b (K -> J3 and Q -> J3);
- neck.

Checks:
- K6 1 mm radial on every pair, especially the rocker vs L2a (they run side by side: assign separate layers);
- the pin-separation rule >= 15 deg (Q-K is at 15: hold it);
- crowns and top faces.

Scratch reference: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-exo-shoulder/029f38fb-570e-5d7a-bebc-fc64e6215529/scratchpad/fb2.py (curve), fb_prox.py (evaluate) and fb2_hyb.py; best configs in hyb2_21.json and hyb2_23.json. Seeds: k21 {a1 40.68, a2 73.76, b 40.12, chi -0.49, gP 17.8, phP 14.48, k 15.0, alq -152.75, sref 188.04}, then a farm CMA with the leader's seat parameters free.
sweep_params: b 25-55, chi -30..+15, gP 15-60, phP -180..180, k 15-50, alq -180..180, sref 0-360, pin radius {5, 7.5}, plus the leader's az, el, a1, a2, wd, wa, q, end_extra. Penalise Q / K pins out of band: the proxy under-weighted them, which is how Q at 0.016 survived the hill climb.
expected_gap: proxy 21.8 (leader 32.9 same proxy); expected 22-27 frozen exact if pin Q can be placed in band; ~27-30 if Q costs its share

name: Spine-parked 3R with the J3 stack inverted (link 2 on hub 3's face plate, arm plate + K7 neck on the cap plate bridging over link 2); watch-scale parts kit merged in
family: spherical 3R (zero passive)
lens: round4:keep J2 / link-2 metal on quiet skin - the arm member must cross link 2's swept annulus, so choose which one sits on top
description: The verified leader spine-parked-j2-3r k7008, metal for metal (three pins meeting at GH: O20 J1 on the acromion top, O15 J2 parked over the posterior acromion / scapular spine, O15 J3 on the lateral deltoid, 12 x 3 Ti links, K7 14 x 6 neck to BOTTOM), with ONE change at hub 3: link 2 is the LOWER member (face plate, F..F+3) and member 3 (arm plate + K7 neck) the UPPER member at F+3.15. The neck leaves the cap plate and bridges over link 2's swept zone (>= 1 mm above it) before dropping to BOTTOM, so link 2 leaves hub 3 at skin level and never climbs over the neck. REST: the neck is a low arch from the hub-3 cap down the lateral arm, link 2 runs under it to J2. OVERHEAD / ACROSS: link 2 swings under the neck root (it used to climb over it). BEHIND-BACK: unchanged. Merged in: watch-scale-spine-3r's parts kit (O11 MR63ZZ-pair J2/J3 micro hubs, 8 x 2 Ti straps) as declared sweep options. Judge measurement: both levers buy ONLY the in-band term, and the layer swap alone already brings frozen in-band to 0.9014 >= 0.90, so the parts kit is worth something only if a re-polish spends in-band slack on reach.
topology: scapula handler -> base -> J1 (ACTIVE R, O20, axis through GH) -> link 1 (12x3 Ti) -> J2 (ACTIVE R, O15, branch -1; link 1 lower, link 2 upper) -> link 2 (12x3 Ti, over link 1) -> J3 (ACTIVE R, O15; link 2 = LOWER face member, member 3 = UPPER cap member) -> member 3 = cap plate + K7 14x6 neck over link 2 and link 1 -> BOTTOM bar -> cuff
components: J1: v5 O20 hub, MR117-2RS pair (7x11x3), 12.25 mm stack. J2, J3: O15 slim hubs, same MR117-2RS pair in a 2.0 mm Ti-6Al-4V wall, bore shoulder + DIN 472 circlip; at J3 the shaft side is member 3 (press-fit O15 cap disc with the O6x2.5 magnet; AS5600 PCB O13 on the link-2 housing). Links 12x3 Ti straps, climb ramps <= 60 deg. Neck K7 14x6 Ti merged with the cut BOTTOM. Sweep options (MVP1 only): O11 hub = MR63ZZ pair (3x6x2.5, catalogue conf "memory") in a 2.5 mm wall, crown ~9; 8x2 Ti straps (469 MPa at 10 N.m in-plane: MVP2 must return to 12x3). No passive part: complexity 0.
why_better: Measured by the proposer at k7008's exact parameters, no retune (judge re-read /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-exo-shoulder/029f38fb-570e-5d7a-bebc-fc64e6215529/scratchpad/lensj2/frz_inv.json vs frz_orig.json): Bench(60,160) fast 28.49 -> 25.55; frozen Bench(110,360) exact 34.29 (reproduces the verifier) -> 32.10 (score 88.3). In-band14 0.878 -> 0.901, link 2 in band 0.795 -> 0.884, neck 0.847 -> 0.807; reach 0.5944, follow 0.9545, contact 0.0154 and collide 0.0031 UNCHANGED. Annulus-crossing law: link 2 rotates about J3 relative to the arm, so any arm-fixed member leaving hub 3 crosses its swept zone unless it exits through a free sector (k7008: 127 deg; crest seats: 20-22 deg); the stacking order is the only choice, and the neck on top pays only where they overlap.
model_spec: Copy docs/concepts/models/spine-parked-j2-3r.py and change build() only: link2 = K.strap_member("link2", p2, p3, ("J2","J3"), width, t, ramp_to=(("hub2", K.STACK), ("hub3", 0.0)), over=[("link1", 1.0)], end_mm=end); neck = K.strap_member("neck", p3, F.H(K.unit(K.BAR0_H)), ("J3",), width=14, t=6, ramp_to=(("hub3", K.STACK),), over=[("link2", 1.0), ("link1", 1.0)]); member list [hubs, link1, link2, neck] so _over sees link 2 first; add a K6 / over entry for the neck vs hub 2's crown. Optional declared parts (from watch-scale-spine-3r): SLIM[5.5] = O11 MR63ZZ pair crown 9.0, SLIM[6.0] = O12 MR85ZZ pair; per-hub crown; strap ramp dz = t_link + 0.15 instead of K.STACK; width/t_link from {12x3, 10x3, 8x2, 6x2}. Checks: dense K2, K6 at 1 mm radial, hub crowns and walls, neck top face vs skin, near-touch (metal < 1 mm = contact), frozen Bench(110,360) exact claim. Red team: neck over link 2 in across-body at elevation 90-150; a base-member stub entering hub 1 through link 1's free sector (k7008: 134 deg toward bvec(146, 46)).
sweep_params: CMA (tools/concept_cma.py, farm) from k7008 with the new layering: az 95-115, el 58-72, a1 34-48, a2 62-80, wd 76-100, wa -25..5, q 0.95-0.99, end_extra 0-4, rad1 {7.5, 8.5, 10}, rad2/rad3 {5.5, 6, 7.5, 8.5}, width/t {12x3, 8x2}, sigma -1, neck width 10-14.
